challenges.title: Matrix chain multiplication
challenges.prompt: Write `matrixChain(dims)`. For matrices A1..An where Ai has shape dims[i-1] x dims[i], return the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to compute the product A1·A2·…·An (any valid parenthesization). Multiplying a p×q by a q×r matrix costs p·q·r. Return 0 if there are fewer than 2 matrices.

challenges.title: Burst balloons
challenges.prompt: Write `maxCoins(nums)`. You have balloons with values `nums`. Bursting balloon i earns `left * nums[i] * right` coins, where left/right are its current neighbours (treat out-of-range as 1). After bursting, its neighbours become adjacent. Return the maximum coins obtainable by bursting all balloons in the best order.

challenges.title: Stone game score difference
challenges.prompt: Write `stoneGameDiff(piles)`. Two players alternate; on each turn a player takes the entire pile from either the left or right end of the row. Both play optimally to maximize their own total. Return (first player's total) − (second player's total).

challenges.title: Travelling salesman (min tour)
challenges.prompt: Write `tsp(dist)` where `dist` is an n×n matrix of non-negative travel costs (n ≤ 10). Starting at city 0, visit every city exactly once and return to city 0. Return the minimum total tour cost. If n = 1, return 0.

challenges.title: Assignment problem
challenges.prompt: Write `minAssignment(cost)` where `cost` is an n×n matrix (n ≤ 10): `cost[w][j]` is the cost of assigning worker w to job j. Assign each worker to a distinct job so every job is used exactly once. Return the minimum total cost.

challenges.title: Digit sum divisible (count)
challenges.prompt: Write `countDigitSumDivisible(n, k)` returning how many integers x in the range 1..n (inclusive) have a decimal digit sum divisible by k. `n` can be as large as 10^12 and k ≥ 1.

challenges.title: Wildcard matching
challenges.prompt: Write `wildcard(s, p)` returning true iff pattern `p` matches the entire string `s`. In `p`, `?` matches any single character and `*` matches any sequence of characters (including empty). All other characters match themselves.

challenges.title: Regular expression matching
challenges.prompt: Write `isMatch(s, p)` returning true iff pattern `p` matches the entire string `s`. In `p`, `.` matches any single character and `*` matches zero or more of the immediately preceding element. Other characters match themselves.

challenges.title: Distinct subsequences (count)
challenges.prompt: Write `distinctSubseq(s, t)` returning the number of distinct subsequences of `s` that equal `t`, modulo 1_000_000_007. A subsequence keeps relative order but need not be contiguous; distinct index sets count separately.

challenges.title: Weighted edit distance
challenges.prompt: Write `weightedEdit(a, b, ci, cd, cs)` returning the minimum cost to transform string `a` into string `b`, where inserting a character costs `ci`, deleting costs `cd`, and substituting one character for a different one costs `cs`. Matching characters cost 0.

challenges.title: Count longest increasing subsequences
challenges.prompt: Write `countLIS(nums)` returning the number of longest strictly increasing subsequences of `nums`. If `nums` is empty, return 0.

challenges.title: Palindrome partitioning min cuts
challenges.prompt: Write `minCut(s)` returning the minimum number of cuts needed so that every resulting substring of `s` is a palindrome. A single-character or empty string needs 0 cuts.

challenges.title: Word break (count segmentations)
challenges.prompt: Write `wordBreakCount(s, dict)` returning the number of ways to segment `s` into a sequence of words all present in `dict` (words may be reused), modulo 1_000_000_007. Return 0 if it cannot be segmented; return 1 for an empty string.

challenges.title: Egg drop (min worst-case trials)
challenges.prompt: Write `eggDrop(eggs, floors)` returning the minimum number of trials that guarantees finding the highest safe floor in a building of `floors` floors using `eggs` identical eggs, in the worst case. A broken egg cannot be reused.

challenges.title: Optimal binary search tree
challenges.prompt: Write `optimalBST(freq)` where `freq[i]` is the access frequency of the i-th key (keys are already sorted). Build a binary search tree minimizing the total cost sum(freq[i] * depth(i)), where the root has depth 1. Return that minimum cost. Return 0 for an empty array.

challenges.title: Count perfect matchings
challenges.prompt: Write `countPerfectMatchings(n, edges)` returning the number of perfect matchings of an undirected graph on vertices 0..n-1 (n even, n ≤ 12). `edges` is a list of `[u, v]` pairs. A perfect matching pairs up all vertices using existing edges, each vertex in exactly one pair.

challenges.title: Two-constraint knapsack
challenges.prompt: Write `knapsack2D(items, W, V)` where each item is `[value, weight, volume]`. Choose a subset (each item at most once) with total weight ≤ W and total volume ≤ V, maximizing total value. Return that maximum value.

challenges.title: Subset sum (count subsets)
challenges.prompt: Write `countSubsetSum(nums, target)` returning the number of subsets of `nums` (each element used at most once) whose elements sum exactly to `target`, modulo 1_000_000_007. The empty subset sums to 0.

challenges.title: Cherry pickup (two robots)
challenges.prompt: Write `cherryPickup(grid)`. Two robots start at the top row: robot A at column 0, robot B at the last column. Both move down one row at a time; each may shift its column by -1, 0, or +1 (staying in bounds). Each cell's value is collected when a robot enters it, but if both robots land on the same cell it is counted only once. Return the maximum total cherries collected when both reach the bottom row.

challenges.title: Dungeon game (min initial health)
challenges.prompt: Write `dungeon(grid)`. A knight starts at the top-left and moves only right or down to reach the bottom-right. Each cell adds its value (possibly negative) to the knight's health. The knight dies if health ever drops to 0 or below. Return the minimum positive integer starting health that lets the knight survive the whole path.

challenges.title: Interleaving string
challenges.prompt: Write `isInterleave(a, b, c)` returning true iff `c` can be formed by interleaving `a` and `b` while preserving the internal order of each. Every character of `a` and `b` must be used exactly once.

challenges.title: Longest palindromic subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `longestPalinSubseq(s)` returning the length of the longest subsequence of `s` that reads the same forwards and backwards (characters need not be contiguous).

challenges.title: Unique paths III (visit all)
challenges.prompt: Write `uniquePathsIII(grid)`. Cells are: 1 = start, 2 = end, 0 = walkable, -1 = obstacle. Moving up/down/left/right, count the number of distinct paths from start to end that walk over every non-obstacle (0) cell exactly once. Return that count.

challenges.title: Partition to k equal-sum subsets
challenges.prompt: Write `canPartitionK(nums, k)` returning true iff `nums` (positive integers) can be split into exactly `k` non-empty groups with equal sums. Every element must be used in exactly one group.

challenges.title: Minimum cost to cut a stick
challenges.prompt: Write `minCostCut(n, cuts)`. A stick spans [0, n]. You must make all cuts at the positions in `cuts` (in any order). The cost of one cut equals the current length of the piece being cut. Return the minimum total cost of performing all cuts.

challenges.title: Stone game II
challenges.prompt: Write `stoneGameII(piles)`. Two players alternate, starting with M = 1. On a turn a player takes the first X piles (1 ≤ X ≤ 2M) from the front; then M becomes max(M, X). The game ends when piles run out. Both maximize their own stones. Return the maximum stones the first player can get.

challenges.title: Distinct palindromic subsequences
challenges.prompt: Write `countPalinSubseq(s)` returning the number of distinct non-empty palindromic subsequences of `s`, modulo 1_000_000_007. Two subsequences are the same if they spell the same string, regardless of which indices were chosen.

challenges.title: Boolean parenthesization (count True)
challenges.prompt: Write `countTrueWays(expr)`. `expr` is a string alternating operands (`T`/`F`) and operators (`&`, `|`, `^`), e.g. `T|F&T`. Return the number of ways to fully parenthesize it so it evaluates to True, modulo 1_000_000_007.

challenges.title: Monotone-digit numbers in a range
challenges.prompt: Write `monotoneInRange(L, R)` returning how many integers x with L ≤ x ≤ R have non-decreasing decimal digits (each digit ≥ the digit before it), e.g. 1357 and 1122 qualify but 1201 does not. 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 10^12.

challenges.title: Cheapest flights within K stops
challenges.prompt: Write `cheapestFlights(n, flights, src, dst, K)`. Cities are 0..n-1; `flights` is a list of `[from, to, price]` directed edges. Return the cheapest total price to go from `src` to `dst` using at most K intermediate stops (a route with K stops uses K+1 flights). Return -1 if unreachable within the limit.

challenges.title: Cheapest flight within K stops
challenges.prompt: Given `n` cities 0..n-1, a directed weighted `flights` list ([u,v,w] with w>0), `src`, `dst`, and `K` (the maximum number of intermediate stops allowed, i.e. at most K+1 edges), return the cheapest total price from src to dst using at most K stops, or -1 if no such route exists. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Shortest path with negative edges
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and a directed weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w], w may be negative but the graph has NO negative cycle), plus `src` and `dst`, return the minimum total weight of a path from src to dst, or null if dst is unreachable. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Minimum spanning tree weight
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w]), return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree. If the graph is not connected (no spanning tree exists), return -1. A single node with no edges has MST weight 0.

challenges.title: Count bridges
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected simple `edges` list (no self-loops or duplicate edges), return the number of bridges: edges whose removal increases the number of connected components. The graph may be disconnected.

challenges.title: Count articulation points
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected simple `edges` list, return the number of articulation points: nodes whose removal increases the number of connected components. The graph may be disconnected.

challenges.title: Number of shortest paths
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1, a directed `edges` list ([u,v] means u->v), and nodes `src`/`dst`, return the number of distinct SHORTEST (fewest-edge) paths from src to dst. Return 0 if dst is unreachable and 1 if src === dst. The answer fits in a 32-bit integer.

challenges.title: Strongly connected components
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and a directed `edges` list ([u,v] means u->v), return the number of strongly connected components (maximal sets where every node can reach every other node in the set).

challenges.title: Expression evaluator (precedence + parens)
challenges.prompt: Evaluate an arithmetic expression string over non-negative integers with operators + - * / and parentheses, honoring standard precedence (* and / bind tighter than + and -) and left-associativity. Division truncates toward zero. Spaces may appear and should be ignored. Return the integer result.

challenges.title: Basic calculator with signed parentheses
challenges.prompt: Evaluate an expression string containing non-negative integers, binary/unary + and -, parentheses, and spaces. A minus sign before a parenthesized group negates the whole group (e.g. 1-(2+3) = -4). Return the integer result.

challenges.title: Nested bracket decode
challenges.prompt: Decode a string encoded as k[substr], meaning substr repeated k times. Encodings may be nested (e.g. 3[a2[c]] = accaccacc). Repeat counts are positive integers that may have MULTIPLE digits. Return the fully decoded string.

challenges.title: Regex matcher with . and *
challenges.prompt: Implement full-string regular expression matching for pattern `p` against string `s`, where '.' matches any single character and '*' matches zero or more of the PRECEDING element. The match must cover the ENTIRE string. Return true or false.

challenges.title: Wildcard matcher with ? and *
challenges.prompt: Implement full-string wildcard matching for pattern `p` against string `s`, where '?' matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters (including the empty sequence). The match must cover the ENTIRE string. Return true or false.

challenges.title: Split on commas with backslash escapes
challenges.prompt: Split a string into fields on commas, where a backslash escapes the following character: a backslash followed by any character contributes that literal character to the current field (so an escaped comma is NOT a separator and an escaped backslash is a literal backslash). A trailing lone backslash contributes a literal backslash. Return the array of decoded field strings.

challenges.title: Longest valid parentheses
challenges.prompt: Given a string of only '(' and ')', return the length of the longest CONTIGUOUS substring that is a well-formed (properly matched) parentheses sequence.

challenges.title: Evaluate reverse Polish notation
challenges.prompt: Evaluate an arithmetic expression given as an array of tokens in reverse Polish (postfix) notation. Tokens are integer strings or one of + - * /. Division truncates toward zero. Return the integer result.

challenges.title: Game of Life after K steps
challenges.prompt: Given a bounded 2D `grid` of 0 (dead) and 1 (live) cells and an integer `K`, apply Conway's Game of Life for exactly K generations (cells outside the grid are always dead) and return the number of live cells remaining. Rules: a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbors survives; a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbors becomes live; all other cells are dead next generation. Neighbors are the 8 surrounding cells.

challenges.title: Shortest-job-first waiting time
challenges.prompt: Given a list of `jobs`, each [arrival, duration], simulate a non-preemptive shortest-job-first scheduler on a single processor: whenever the processor is free, among all jobs that have arrived and not yet run, start the one with the smallest duration (ties: smaller arrival, then smaller original index); if none have arrived, idle until the next arrival. Return the total waiting time summed over all jobs, where a job's waiting time is (start time − arrival time).

challenges.title: Convex hull vertex count
challenges.prompt: Given a list of distinct integer-coordinate `points` [x,y], return the number of vertices (true corners) of their convex hull. Points that lie strictly inside the hull, and collinear points lying on the interior of a hull edge, are NOT counted — only actual corners. For 1 or 2 points, return the number of points.

challenges.title: Interior lattice points of a polygon
challenges.prompt: Given a simple polygon as an ordered list of integer-coordinate vertices `poly` [x,y], return the number of lattice (integer) points strictly inside the polygon, using Pick's theorem. (Interior points I = Area − Boundary/2 + 1, where Boundary counts all integer points on the edges.)

challenges.title: Count intersecting segment pairs
challenges.prompt: Given a list of `segments`, each [x1,y1,x2,y2] with integer endpoints, return the number of unordered pairs (i<j) of segments that intersect. Two segments intersect if they share at least one point, INCLUDING touching at an endpoint or overlapping while collinear.

challenges.title: Max points on a line
challenges.prompt: Given a list of integer-coordinate `points` [x,y] (duplicates allowed), return the maximum number of points that lie on a single straight line. Identical points all count as lying on every line through that location.

challenges.title: Closest pair squared distance
challenges.prompt: Given a list of integer-coordinate `points` [x,y] (at least two, duplicates allowed), return the minimum squared Euclidean distance between any two distinct entries in the list.

challenges.title: Boolean expression evaluator
challenges.prompt: Evaluate a boolean expression string over literals 0 and 1 with operators ! (NOT, unary, highest precedence), & (AND), and | (OR, lowest precedence), plus parentheses and optional spaces. Precedence is ! > & > |, and & / | are left-associative. Return 1 for true or 0 for false.

challenges.title: All-pairs shortest path query
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and a directed weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w], weights may be negative but there is no negative cycle), plus `src` and `dst`, return the shortest total path weight from src to dst, or null if unreachable. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Round-robin completion order
challenges.prompt: Given an array of `bursts` (CPU time each process needs, all arriving at time 0) and a time `quantum`, simulate round-robin scheduling: process indices 0..n-1 start in a ready queue in index order; repeatedly take the front process, run it for min(quantum, remaining) time, and if it still has work left append it to the back. Return the array of process indices in the order they COMPLETE.

challenges.title: Expression with right-associative power
challenges.prompt: Evaluate an arithmetic expression over non-negative integers with operators + (add), * (multiply), and ^ (exponentiation), plus parentheses and optional spaces. Precedence is ^ > * > +; ^ is RIGHT-associative (2^3^2 = 2^(3^2)) while + and * are left-associative. Inputs are chosen so the exact integer result is within safe range. Return the integer result.

challenges.title: Minimax bottleneck path
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1, an undirected weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w], w>0), and nodes `src`/`dst`, return the minimum possible value of the MAXIMUM edge weight along any path from src to dst (the bottleneck), or -1 if dst is unreachable. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Detect any negative cycle
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and a directed weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w], weights may be negative; self-loops allowed), return true if the graph contains ANY negative-weight cycle (reachable from any node), else false.

challenges.title: Min cost to connect all points (Manhattan)
challenges.prompt: Given a list of integer-coordinate `points` [x,y], return the minimum total cost to connect all points into one network, where the cost of an edge between two points is their Manhattan distance |dx| + |dy|. With 0 or 1 points the cost is 0.

challenges.title: Count topological orderings
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 (n <= 10) and a directed `edges` list ([u,v] means u must come before v), return the number of distinct valid topological orderings of all nodes. If the graph has a cycle (no valid ordering), return 0.

challenges.title: Minimum coins
challenges.prompt: Write `minCoins(coins, amount)` returning the fewest coins (unlimited supply of each denomination) that sum exactly to `amount`, or -1 if impossible.

challenges.title: Coin change combinations
challenges.prompt: Write `changeWays(coins, amount)` returning the number of distinct combinations of coins (unlimited supply) that sum to `amount`. Combinations that differ only in order count once.

challenges.title: Longest increasing subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `lengthOfLIS(nums)` returning the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence (elements need not be contiguous).

challenges.title: Longest common subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `lcs(a, b)` returning the length of the longest common subsequence of strings `a` and `b`.

challenges.title: Edit distance
challenges.prompt: Write `editDistance(a, b)` returning the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, or substitutions to turn `a` into `b`.

challenges.title: 0/1 knapsack
challenges.prompt: Write `knapsack(weights, values, capacity)` returning the maximum total value of a subset of items whose total weight does not exceed `capacity`. Each item may be used at most once.

challenges.title: Unbounded knapsack
challenges.prompt: Write `unboundedKnapsack(weights, values, capacity)` returning the maximum total value where each item may be used any number of times, subject to total weight <= `capacity`.

challenges.title: Partition equal subset sum
challenges.prompt: Write `canPartition(nums)` returning true if the array (non-negative integers) can be split into two subsets with equal sums, else false.

challenges.title: Subset sum
challenges.prompt: Write `subsetSum(nums, target)` returning true if some subset of `nums` (non-negative integers) sums exactly to `target`, else false.

challenges.title: Minimum path sum
challenges.prompt: Write `minPathSum(grid)` where you start at the top-left and move only right or down to the bottom-right. Return the minimum sum of the values on the path.

challenges.title: Unique paths with obstacles
challenges.prompt: Write `uniquePaths(grid)` counting the number of distinct top-left to bottom-right paths moving only right or down. Cells with value 1 are obstacles and cannot be entered (0 is free). If the start or end cell is an obstacle, the answer is 0.

challenges.title: Word break
challenges.prompt: Write `wordBreak(s, dict)` returning true if `s` can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more words from the array `dict` (each word reusable).

challenges.title: Decode ways
challenges.prompt: Write `numDecodings(s)` counting the ways to decode a digit string into letters where '1'->A .. '26'->Z. A leading zero in a group is invalid ('0','06' decode to nothing). Return the number of valid decodings.

challenges.title: Palindrome min cuts
challenges.prompt: Write `minCut(s)` returning the minimum number of cuts needed so every resulting substring is a palindrome.

challenges.title: Count palindromic substrings
challenges.prompt: Write `countPalindromes(s)` returning the number of palindromic substrings of `s` (substrings at different start/end positions count separately, single characters included).

challenges.title: House robber
challenges.prompt: Write `rob(nums)` returning the maximum total you can take from a row of houses without taking two adjacent houses.

challenges.title: House robber (circular)
challenges.prompt: Write `robCircular(nums)` for houses arranged in a circle (first and last are adjacent). Return the maximum total with no two adjacent houses taken.

challenges.title: Maximum product subarray
challenges.prompt: Write `maxProduct(nums)` returning the largest product of any contiguous non-empty subarray.

challenges.title: Max circular subarray sum
challenges.prompt: Write `maxCircularSum(nums)` returning the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray of a circular array (the subarray may wrap from the end to the beginning, but uses each element at most once).

challenges.title: Stock trading (k transactions)
challenges.prompt: Write `maxProfit(prices, k)` returning the maximum profit from at most `k` buy-sell transactions. You must sell before buying again (no overlapping positions).

challenges.title: Stock trading (cooldown)
challenges.prompt: Write `maxProfitCooldown(prices)`. Unlimited transactions, but after you sell you must wait one day (cooldown) before buying again. Return the maximum profit.

challenges.title: Stock trading (fee)
challenges.prompt: Write `maxProfitFee(prices, fee)`. Unlimited transactions, but each completed buy-sell pair costs `fee`. Return the maximum profit.

challenges.title: Domino & tromino tiling
challenges.prompt: Write `numTilings(n)` returning the number of ways to tile a 2xN board with 2x1 dominoes and L-shaped trominoes (each tromino covers three cells in an L). Rotations/reflections of a piece are allowed. Return the count modulo 1000000007.

challenges.title: Min cost climbing stairs
challenges.prompt: Write `minCostClimb(cost)`. From step i you may climb 1 or 2 steps, paying cost[i] to leave step i. You may start at index 0 or 1. Return the minimum cost to go past the last step.

challenges.title: Longest palindromic subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `lps(s)` returning the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of `s` (characters need not be contiguous).

challenges.title: Count of LIS
challenges.prompt: Write `countLIS(nums)` returning the number of longest strictly increasing subsequences in `nums`.

challenges.title: Russian doll envelopes
challenges.prompt: Write `maxEnvelopes(envelopes)` where each envelope is [w, h]. One fits inside another only if both its width and height are strictly greater. Return the maximum number that can be nested.

challenges.title: Rod cutting
challenges.prompt: Write `rodCut(prices, n)` where prices[i] is the value of a piece of length i+1. Cut a rod of length `n` into integer pieces to maximize total value. Return the max value.

challenges.title: Matrix chain multiplication
challenges.prompt: Write `matrixChain(dims)` where matrix i has dimensions dims[i] x dims[i+1]. Return the minimum number of scalar multiplications to multiply the whole chain.

challenges.title: Longest arithmetic subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `longestArithSeq(nums)` returning the length of the longest subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) whose consecutive elements have a constant difference.

challenges.title: Maximal square
challenges.prompt: Write `maximalSquare(matrix)` on a grid of 0s and 1s. Return the area (side*side) of the largest square sub-grid consisting entirely of 1s.

challenges.title: Minimum falling path sum
challenges.prompt: Write `minFallingPath(matrix)` (square grid). A falling path starts in any cell of the first row and each step moves to the cell directly below, below-left, or below-right. Return the minimum path sum.

challenges.title: Triangle minimum path
challenges.prompt: Write `minTrianglePath(triangle)` (array of rows, row i has i+1 elements). Start at the top; each step moves to one of the two adjacent numbers on the row below. Return the minimum top-to-bottom path sum.

challenges.title: Interleaving string
challenges.prompt: Write `isInterleave(a, b, c)` returning true if `c` can be formed by interleaving the characters of `a` and `b` while preserving the relative order within each.

challenges.title: Distinct subsequences
challenges.prompt: Write `numDistinct(s, t)` returning the number of distinct subsequences of `s` that equal `t`.

challenges.title: Wildcard matching
challenges.prompt: Write `isMatch(s, p)` where pattern `p` may contain '?' (matches any single character) and '*' (matches any sequence, including empty). Return true if `p` matches the entire string `s`.

challenges.title: Burst balloons
challenges.prompt: Write `maxCoins(nums)`. Bursting balloon i earns nums[left]*nums[i]*nums[right] coins, where left/right are the adjacent still-unburst balloons (out-of-range neighbors count as 1). Return the maximum coins from bursting all balloons.

challenges.title: Longest common substring
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonSubstring(a, b)` returning the length of the longest string that appears as a *contiguous* substring of both `a` and `b`.

challenges.title: Perfect squares
challenges.prompt: Write `numSquares(n)` returning the least number of perfect-square numbers (1,4,9,16,...) that sum to `n`.

challenges.title: Integer break
challenges.prompt: Write `integerBreak(n)` (n >= 2). Break `n` into the sum of at least two positive integers and return the maximum possible product of those integers.

challenges.title: Target sum ways
challenges.prompt: Write `targetSumWays(nums, target)` counting the ways to assign a + or - sign to each number (non-negative integers) so the signed sum equals `target`.

challenges.title: Ones and zeroes
challenges.prompt: Write `findMaxForm(strs, m, n)` where `strs` is an array of binary strings. Return the size of the largest subset such that the subset uses at most `m` zeros and `n` ones in total.

challenges.title: Combination sum (ordered)
challenges.prompt: Write `combinationSum4(nums, target)` counting the number of ordered sequences of numbers from `nums` (distinct positive integers, each reusable) that sum to `target`. Different orderings count as different sequences.

challenges.title: Delete and earn
challenges.prompt: Write `deleteAndEarn(nums)`. Repeatedly pick a value v: you earn v times its count, but must delete every element equal to v-1 and v+1. Return the maximum total points.

challenges.title: Stone game score difference
challenges.prompt: Write `stoneGameDiff(piles)`. Two players alternate; each turn a player takes the whole pile from either the left or right end, adding it to their score. Both play to maximize their own score. Return (first player's score) - (second player's score) under optimal play.

challenges.title: Sum of an array
challenges.prompt: Write `sumArray(nums)` returning the sum of all numbers in the array. The sum of an empty array is 0.

challenges.title: Maximum of an array
challenges.prompt: Write `maxArray(nums)` returning the largest number in the non-empty array.

challenges.title: Minimum of an array
challenges.prompt: Write `minArray(nums)` returning the smallest number in the non-empty array.

challenges.title: Count vowels
challenges.prompt: Write `countVowels(str)` returning the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in the string, case-insensitive.

challenges.title: Is palindrome
challenges.prompt: Write `isPalindrome(str)` returning true if the string reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring letter case.

challenges.title: Factorial
challenges.prompt: Write `factorial(n)` returning n! for a non-negative integer n. By definition 0! is 1.

challenges.title: Is odd
challenges.prompt: Write `isOdd(n)` returning true if the integer n is odd, false otherwise. Works for negative integers too.

challenges.title: Average of an array
challenges.prompt: Write `average(nums)` returning the arithmetic mean of the array. The average of an empty array is 0.

challenges.title: Count occurrences
challenges.prompt: Write `countOccurrences(arr, x)` returning how many times x appears in the array.

challenges.title: Capitalize first letter
challenges.prompt: Write `capitalizeFirst(str)` returning the string with its first character uppercased. An empty string returns an empty string.

challenges.title: Count words
challenges.prompt: Write `countWords(str)` returning the number of whitespace-separated words. An empty or all-whitespace string has 0 words.

challenges.title: Sum of even numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `sumEvens(nums)` returning the sum of all even numbers in the array (including negatives and zero).

challenges.title: Count positive numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `countPositives(nums)` returning how many numbers are strictly greater than zero.

challenges.title: Deduplicate array
challenges.prompt: Write `dedupe(arr)` returning a new array with duplicates removed, keeping each element's first-seen order.

challenges.title: Nth Fibonacci
challenges.prompt: Write `fibonacci(n)` returning the nth Fibonacci number where fibonacci(0)=0, fibonacci(1)=1.

challenges.title: Is prime
challenges.prompt: Write `isPrime(n)` returning true if the integer n is prime. Numbers below 2 are not prime.

challenges.title: Count digits
challenges.prompt: Write `digitCount(n)` returning how many digits the integer n has (a leading minus sign is not a digit).

challenges.title: Sign of a number
challenges.prompt: Write `sign(n)` returning 1 if n is positive, -1 if negative, and 0 if it is zero.

challenges.title: Count negative numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `countNegatives(nums)` returning how many numbers are strictly less than zero.

challenges.title: Product of an array
challenges.prompt: Write `product(nums)` returning the product of all numbers. The product of an empty array is 1.

challenges.title: Contains duplicate
challenges.prompt: Write `containsDuplicate(arr)` returning true if any value appears at least twice, false if all values are distinct.

challenges.title: Remove all of an element
challenges.prompt: Write `removeElement(arr, x)` returning a new array with every occurrence of x removed, order preserved.

challenges.title: Count a character
challenges.prompt: Write `countChar(str, ch)` returning how many times the single character ch appears in str.

challenges.title: All positive
challenges.prompt: Write `allPositive(nums)` returning true if every number is strictly greater than zero. An empty array counts as true.

challenges.title: Even or odd label
challenges.prompt: Write `evenOrOdd(n)` returning the string "even" or "odd" for the integer n. Works for negatives.

challenges.title: Is a vowel
challenges.prompt: Write `isVowel(ch)` returning true if the single character ch is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u), case-insensitive.

challenges.title: Count uppercase letters
challenges.prompt: Write `countUpper(str)` returning how many characters are uppercase letters A-Z (spaces and digits do not count).

challenges.title: Sum of odd numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `sumOddNumbers(nums)` returning the sum of all odd numbers in the array (including negatives).

challenges.title: Longest string length
challenges.prompt: Write `maxLength(words)` returning the length of the longest string in the array. An empty array returns 0.

challenges.title: Remove spaces
challenges.prompt: Write `removeSpaces(str)` returning the string with all space characters removed.

challenges.title: Is positive
challenges.prompt: Write `isPositive(n)` returning true if n is strictly greater than zero, false otherwise.

challenges.title: Sum of first N
challenges.prompt: Write `sumFirstN(arr, n)` returning the sum of the first n elements. If n exceeds the array length, sum only the elements that exist.

challenges.title: Sum of squares
challenges.prompt: Write `sumSquares(nums)` returning the sum of the squares of the numbers. An empty array returns 0.

challenges.title: Letter grade
challenges.prompt: Write `gradeLetter(score)` returning "A" for score>=90, "B" for >=80, "C" for >=70, "D" for >=60, else "F".

challenges.title: Clamp to range
challenges.prompt: Write `clamp(x, lo, hi)` returning x limited to the range [lo, hi]: lo if x<lo, hi if x>hi, otherwise x.

challenges.title: Count greater than
challenges.prompt: Write `countGreater(nums, x)` returning how many numbers are strictly greater than x.

challenges.title: Last index of
challenges.prompt: Write `lastIndexOf(arr, x)` returning the index of the last occurrence of x, or -1 if x is not present.

challenges.title: Sum of multiples of 3
challenges.prompt: Write `sumMultiplesOf3(nums)` returning the sum of all numbers divisible by 3 (including 0 and negatives).

challenges.title: Count unique values
challenges.prompt: Write `countUnique(arr)` returning the number of distinct values in the array.

challenges.title: Starts with a vowel
challenges.prompt: Write `startsWithVowel(word)` returning true if the word's first letter is a vowel (case-insensitive). An empty string returns false.

challenges.title: Run-length encode
challenges.prompt: Write `rleEncode(s)` that run-length encodes a string: each maximal run of a repeated character becomes the run length (in decimal) immediately followed by the character. A run of length 1 is written as `1` then the character. Return the encoded string (empty string stays empty).

challenges.title: Run-length decode
challenges.prompt: Write `rleDecode(s)` that decodes a run-length encoded string of the form (decimal count)(character) repeated, e.g. `"3a2b1c"`. Counts may have multiple digits (e.g. `"12a"` means 12 `a`s). Return the decoded string.

challenges.title: Run-length decoded length
challenges.prompt: Write `rleDecodeLength(s)` returning the length of the string that the run-length encoding `s` decodes to, without necessarily building it. `s` is a sequence of (decimal count)(character) pairs; counts may span several digits.

challenges.title: Decode length-prefixed list
challenges.prompt: Write `decodeList(s)` that decodes a string produced by concatenating, for each original string, its length in decimal, a `#`, then the string itself (e.g. `"3#abc2#de"`). Lengths may be multi-digit; contents may contain `#`. Return the array of decoded strings.

challenges.title: Length-prefixed encoded size
challenges.prompt: Write `encodedLength(strs)` returning the total length of the string obtained by concatenating, for each element, its length in decimal, a `#`, then the element. Do not build the string; just compute the size. `strs` is an array of strings.

challenges.title: Zigzag conversion
challenges.prompt: Write `zigzagConvert(s, numRows)` that writes `s` in a zigzag pattern across `numRows` rows (down then diagonally up, repeating) and returns the string read row by row. When `numRows` is 1 the string is unchanged.

challenges.title: Group shifted strings (count)
challenges.prompt: Two strings belong to the same group if one can be turned into the other by shifting every letter by the same amount with wraparound (`z`→`a`). Write `groupShiftedStringsCount(strs)` returning the number of distinct groups. Strings of different lengths are never in the same group.

challenges.title: Largest shifted group
challenges.prompt: Write `largestShiftedGroup(strs)` returning the size of the largest group of shift-equivalent strings (one becomes another by shifting every letter by the same amount, wrapping `z`→`a`). Different lengths never share a group. Return 0 for an empty array.

challenges.title: Excel column title
challenges.prompt: Write `columnToTitle(n)` converting a 1-based column number to its spreadsheet title: 1→`"A"`, 26→`"Z"`, 27→`"AA"`, 28→`"AB"`, and so on.

challenges.title: Excel title to column
challenges.prompt: Write `titleToColumn(s)` converting a spreadsheet column title (`"A"`, `"AA"`, `"ZZ"`, ...) to its 1-based column number: `"A"`→1, `"Z"`→26, `"AA"`→27.

challenges.title: Integer to English words
challenges.prompt: Write `numberToWords(n)` for `0 <= n <= 9999`, returning the English words with each word capitalized and single-space separated, e.g. 0→`"Zero"`, 123→`"One Hundred Twenty Three"`, 1000→`"One Thousand"`, 1015→`"One Thousand Fifteen"`. No hyphens, no `"and"`.

challenges.title: Decode ways with wildcard
challenges.prompt: Letters map `A`=1..`Z`=26. A `*` stands for any single digit 1-9. Write `numDecodingsStar(s)` returning the exact number of ways to decode `s` (a string of digits and `*`). `0` alone is invalid; a leading `0` in a pair is invalid. Return an integer (inputs are bounded so the count fits a safe integer).

challenges.title: Decode ways
challenges.prompt: Letters map `A`=1..`Z`=26. Write `numDecodings(s)` returning the number of ways to decode the digit string `s`. A `0` cannot stand alone and can only appear as the second digit of `10` or `20`. Return an integer.

challenges.title: Longest back-reference
challenges.prompt: For an LZ-style compressor, write `longestBackref(s)` returning the length of the longest substring that occurs starting at two different positions in `s` (occurrences may overlap). Return 0 if no character repeats.

challenges.title: Delta encode
challenges.prompt: Write `deltaEncode(nums)` returning an array whose first element equals `nums[0]` and each later element is the difference from the previous original value (`nums[i]-nums[i-1]`). Return `[]` for an empty input.

challenges.title: Delta decode
challenges.prompt: Write `deltaDecode(deltas)` inverting delta encoding: the first element is the starting value and each later element is added to the running total to reconstruct the originals. Return `[]` for an empty input.

challenges.title: Base conversion (digit arrays)
challenges.prompt: Write `baseConvert(digits, fromBase, toBase)` where `digits` is an array of digit values (most significant first) representing a number in `fromBase`. Return the array of digit values (most significant first) in `toBase`. Use `[0]` for zero; otherwise no leading zeros.

challenges.title: Unique Morse representations
challenges.prompt: Each lowercase letter maps to a Morse code (`a`=".-", `b`="-...", ... `z`="--.."). A word's transformation is the concatenation of its letters' codes with no separators. Write `uniqueMorse(words)` returning the number of distinct transformations among `words`.

challenges.title: Run-length pairs
challenges.prompt: Write `rleEncodePairs(s)` returning an array of `[character, runLength]` pairs, one per maximal run of equal characters, in order. Distinct runs of the same character (separated by others) stay separate. Return `[]` for an empty string.

challenges.title: Huffman total encoded length
challenges.prompt: Given `freqs`, an array of positive symbol frequencies (length >= 2), write `huffmanTotalLength(freqs)` returning the total number of bits of an optimal (Huffman) prefix code: the sum over symbols of frequency times code length. Equivalently, the sum of the values combined at each merge step.

challenges.title: Base-N string to decimal
challenges.prompt: Write `baseToDecimal(s, base)` parsing the string `s` (digits `0-9` and lowercase/uppercase `a-f`) as a number in the given `base` (2..16) and returning its decimal value. Inputs fit a safe integer.

challenges.title: Decimal to base-N string
challenges.prompt: Write `decimalToBase(num, base)` returning the string representation of non-negative integer `num` in `base` (2..16), using lowercase `a-f` for values 10-15. `0` returns `"0"`; no leading zeros otherwise.

challenges.title: Next Excel column
challenges.prompt: Write `nextColumn(title)` returning the spreadsheet column title immediately after `title`: `"A"`→`"B"`, `"Z"`→`"AA"`, `"AZ"`→`"BA"`, `"ZZ"`→`"AAA"`.

challenges.title: Zigzag row lengths
challenges.prompt: Write `zigzagRowLengths(len, numRows)` returning an array with the number of characters that land in each row when a string of length `len` is written in the standard zigzag pattern over `numRows` rows. When `numRows` is 1 the result is `[len]`.

challenges.title: Add binary strings
challenges.prompt: Write `addBinary(a, b)` returning the binary string sum of two binary strings. Handle arbitrarily long inputs (do not rely on native integer conversion). No leading zeros except the string `"0"` itself.

challenges.title: Canonical shift form
challenges.prompt: Write `canonicalShift(s)` returning the canonical form of a lowercase string under letter-shifting: shift every character so the first becomes `a`, wrapping `z`→`a`. Shift-equivalent strings share the same canonical form. Return `""` for the empty string.

challenges.title: Count runs
challenges.prompt: Write `countRuns(s)` returning the number of maximal runs of equal consecutive characters in `s` (i.e. the number of tokens a run-length encoder would emit). Return 0 for the empty string.

challenges.title: Run-length encoded size
challenges.prompt: Write `rleSize(s)` returning the length of the run-length encoded form of `s`, where each run contributes the number of digits of its length plus one (for the character). Do not build the encoding. Return 0 for the empty string.

challenges.title: Palindrome in base
challenges.prompt: Write `isPalindromeInBase(num, base)` returning `true` if the representation of non-negative integer `num` in the given `base` (2..16) reads the same forwards and backwards, else `false`. Zero is a palindrome.

challenges.title: Zigzag varint encode
challenges.prompt: Write `zigzagEncode(n)` mapping a signed integer to a non-negative integer using zigzag encoding: non-negative `n` maps to `2*n`, negative `n` maps to `-2*n - 1`. So 0→0, -1→1, 1→2, -2→3, 2→4.

challenges.title: Merge intervals
challenges.prompt: Write `mergeIntervals(intervals)` where `intervals` is an array of `[start, end]` pairs (not necessarily sorted). Return the list of merged, non-overlapping intervals sorted by start. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint (e.g. `[1,4]` and `[4,5]`) merge into one.

challenges.title: Insert interval
challenges.prompt: Write `insertInterval(intervals, newInterval)`. `intervals` is a list of non-overlapping `[start,end]` pairs sorted by start. Insert `newInterval` (a `[start,end]` pair), merging as needed, and return the resulting sorted non-overlapping list. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint merge into one.

challenges.title: Can attend all meetings
challenges.prompt: Write `canAttendAll(meetings)` where `meetings` is a list of `[start,end]` pairs. Return `true` if one person can attend every meeting (no two overlap). A meeting ending exactly when another starts does NOT conflict.

challenges.title: Minimum meeting rooms
challenges.prompt: Write `minMeetingRooms(meetings)` where `meetings` is a list of `[start,end]` pairs. Return the minimum number of rooms needed so that no two meetings sharing a room overlap. A meeting ending exactly when another starts can reuse the same room.

challenges.title: Minimum arrows to burst balloons
challenges.prompt: Write `findMinArrows(points)` where `points` is a list of `[start,end]` balloon spans. An arrow shot at x bursts every balloon with `start <= x <= end`. Return the minimum number of arrows to burst all balloons. Balloons touching at an endpoint (e.g. `[1,2]` and `[2,3]`) can be burst by a single arrow.

challenges.title: Non-overlapping intervals (min removals)
challenges.prompt: Write `eraseOverlap(intervals)` returning the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest are non-overlapping. `intervals` is a list of `[start,end]` pairs. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint are NOT considered overlapping.

challenges.title: Activity selection (max non-overlapping)
challenges.prompt: Write `maxActivities(activities)` returning the maximum number of pairwise non-overlapping activities you can keep. `activities` is a list of `[start,end]` pairs. Two activities may share an endpoint (one ends exactly when the next starts).

challenges.title: Interval list intersections
challenges.prompt: Write `intervalIntersection(A, B)` where `A` and `B` are each a list of pairwise-disjoint `[start,end]` intervals sorted by start. Return the list of their intersections, sorted by start. Intervals touching at a single point yield a degenerate intersection like `[5,5]`.

challenges.title: Remove covered intervals
challenges.prompt: Write `removeCovered(intervals)` returning how many intervals remain after removing every interval that is covered by another. Interval `[a,b]` is covered by `[c,d]` if `c <= a` and `b <= d`. `intervals` is a list of `[start,end]` pairs; two intervals may share a start.

challenges.title: Largest number
challenges.prompt: Write `largestNumber(nums)` where `nums` is an array of non-negative integers. Arrange them so their concatenation forms the largest possible number, and return it as a string. If the result would be all zeros, return "0".

challenges.title: Gas station circuit
challenges.prompt: Write `canCompleteCircuit(gas, cost)`. There are `gas.length` stations in a circle; `gas[i]` is fuel available at station i and `cost[i]` is fuel needed to travel from i to i+1. Starting with an empty tank at some station, return the index of the station from which you can complete the full circuit, or `-1` if impossible. If a solution exists it is unique.

challenges.title: Jump game (reachability)
challenges.prompt: Write `canJump(nums)` where `nums[i]` is the maximum forward jump length from index i. Starting at index 0, return `true` if you can reach the last index. An empty array counts as reachable (`true`).

challenges.title: Jump game II (min jumps)
challenges.prompt: Write `minJumps(nums)` where `nums[i]` is the maximum forward jump length from index i. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index from index 0 (the last index is always reachable). An array of length 0 or 1 needs 0 jumps.

challenges.title: Partition labels
challenges.prompt: Write `partitionLabels(s)` for a lowercase string `s`. Partition `s` into as many contiguous parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return an array of the part lengths, in order. The empty string returns `[]`.

challenges.title: Task scheduler (cooldown)
challenges.prompt: Write `leastInterval(tasks, n)`. `tasks` is an array of task labels; identical tasks must be separated by at least `n` intervals of cooldown (during which the CPU may run a different task or stay idle). Return the least number of intervals the CPU needs to finish all tasks. Empty `tasks` needs 0 intervals.

challenges.title: Candy distribution
challenges.prompt: Write `candy(ratings)`. Each child (in a row) gets at least one candy, and any child with a strictly higher rating than an adjacent child must get more candies than that neighbor. Return the minimum total candies. Empty input returns 0.

challenges.title: Two city scheduling (min cost)
challenges.prompt: Write `twoCitySchedCost(costs)` where `costs[i] = [costA, costB]` is the cost of flying person i to city A or city B. Exactly half the people must go to each city. Return the minimum total cost. The number of people is always even.

challenges.title: Job sequencing with deadlines
challenges.prompt: Write `jobScheduling(jobs)` where `jobs[i] = [deadline, profit]`. Each job takes one unit of time and must run in an integer slot within `1..deadline`; only one job runs per slot. Return the maximum total profit obtainable.

challenges.title: Sort by frequency then value
challenges.prompt: Write `frequencySort(nums)` returning the integers sorted so that less frequent values come first; values with the same frequency are ordered from larger to smaller. Every occurrence is kept in the output.

challenges.title: Minimum railway platforms
challenges.prompt: Write `minPlatforms(arr, dep)` where `arr[i]` and `dep[i]` are the arrival and departure times of train i. Return the minimum number of platforms so no train waits. A platform can be reused for a new train only if the previous train departed strictly before the new one arrives (equal times need separate platforms).

challenges.title: Queue reconstruction by height
challenges.prompt: Write `reconstructQueue(people)` where `people[i] = [h, k]` means a person of height `h` with exactly `k` people of height greater than or equal to `h` standing in front of them. Return any valid queue as a list of `[h,k]` — reconstructed by the standard tallest-first insertion, which yields a unique canonical arrangement.

challenges.title: Boats to save people
challenges.prompt: Write `numRescueBoats(people, limit)` where `people[i]` is a weight. Each boat carries at most two people with combined weight at most `limit`. Return the minimum number of boats to carry everyone.

challenges.title: Assign cookies
challenges.prompt: Write `findContentChildren(greed, size)`. Child i is content if given a cookie of size at least `greed[i]`; each cookie feeds at most one child. Return the maximum number of content children.

challenges.title: Minimum cost to connect ropes
challenges.prompt: Write `connectRopes(ropes)`. Repeatedly combine two ropes into one at a cost equal to the sum of their lengths, until a single rope remains. Return the minimum total cost. Zero or one rope costs 0.

challenges.title: Maximum events attended
challenges.prompt: Write `maxEvents(events)` where `events[i] = [start, end]` (inclusive day range, days start at 1). You can attend at most one event per day, and each event on any single day within its range. Return the maximum number of events you can attend.

challenges.title: Carpooling capacity
challenges.prompt: Write `carPooling(trips, capacity)` where `trips[i] = [numPassengers, from, to]`. Passengers board at `from` and leave at `to` (they are NOT in the car at location `to`). The car only drives forward. Return `true` if all trips fit without ever exceeding `capacity`.

challenges.title: Maximum length of pair chain
challenges.prompt: Write `findLongestChain(pairs)` where `pairs[i] = [a, b]` with `a < b`. Pair `(c,d)` can follow `(a,b)` only if `b < c`. Return the length of the longest chain that can be formed (pairs may be used in any order).

challenges.title: Wiggle subsequence length
challenges.prompt: Write `wiggleMaxLength(nums)` returning the length of the longest wiggle subsequence: a sequence whose successive differences strictly alternate between positive and negative. Equal adjacent values do not count as a wiggle. Fewer than two elements is trivially a wiggle.

challenges.title: Maximum units on a truck
challenges.prompt: Write `maximumUnits(boxTypes, truckSize)` where `boxTypes[i] = [numberOfBoxes, unitsPerBox]`. Load at most `truckSize` boxes total onto the truck to maximize total units. Return the maximum units.

challenges.title: Coin change (minimum coins)
challenges.prompt: Write `minCoinsChange(coins, amount)` returning the fewest coins that sum exactly to `amount`, or `-1` if impossible. You have an unlimited supply of each coin denomination.

challenges.title: Reduce array size to half
challenges.prompt: Write `minSetSize(arr)`. Choose a set of integers and remove every occurrence of each chosen integer, so that at least half of the array is removed. Return the minimum number of distinct integers you must choose.

challenges.title: Maximum ice cream bars
challenges.prompt: Write `maxIceCream(costs, coins)` where `costs[i]` is the price of bar i and `coins` is your budget. Return the maximum number of bars you can buy (each bar at most once).

challenges.title: Sort fractions ascending
challenges.prompt: Write `fractionSort(fracs)` where `fracs[i] = [numerator, denominator]` with `denominator > 0`. Return the fractions sorted in ascending order of value (compare exactly, without floating-point rounding error).

challenges.title: Maximize sum after K negations
challenges.prompt: Write `largestSumAfterKNegations(nums, k)`. You must perform exactly `k` operations; each operation picks an index and negates that element (indices may be reused). Return the largest possible sum of the array afterward.

challenges.title: Lemonade change
challenges.prompt: Write `lemonadeChange(bills)` where each customer pays with a 5, 10, or 20 bill for a 5-dollar lemonade and you must give correct change. You start with no cash and serve customers in order. Return `true` if you can give every customer correct change.

challenges.title: Minimum refueling stops
challenges.prompt: Write `minRefuelStops(target, startFuel, stations)` where `stations[i] = [position, fuel]` is sorted by position. The car starts with `startFuel` and uses one unit of fuel per unit distance. At a reachable station you may refuel (adding its fuel). Return the minimum number of refueling stops to reach `target`, or `-1` if impossible.

challenges.title: Minimum increments to make unique
challenges.prompt: Write `minIncrementForUnique(nums)` returning the minimum total number of +1 increments needed so that every value in the array is distinct.

challenges.title: Best time to buy and sell stock II
challenges.prompt: Write `maxProfit(prices)` where `prices[i]` is the price on day i. You may buy and sell as many times as you like (but must sell before buying again). Return the maximum total profit.

challenges.title: Container with most water
challenges.prompt: Write `maxArea(height)` where `height[i]` is the height of a vertical line at position i. Choose two lines that, with the x-axis, form a container holding the most water. Return that maximum area (`min(height[i],height[j]) * (j - i)`).

challenges.title: Trapping rain water
challenges.prompt: Write `trap(height)` where `height[i]` is an elevation. Return the total units of rain water trapped between the bars after it rains.

challenges.title: Non-decreasing with one change
challenges.prompt: Write `checkPossibility(nums)` returning `true` if the array can be made non-decreasing by modifying at most one element (to any value).

challenges.title: Maximum distance to closest person
challenges.prompt: Write `maxDistToClosest(seats)` where `seats[i]` is 1 if occupied and 0 if empty (there is at least one of each). If you sit in the best empty seat, return the maximum possible distance to the nearest occupied seat.

challenges.title: Split array largest sum
challenges.prompt: Write `splitArray(nums, k)` where `nums` are non-negative integers. Split the array into `k` non-empty contiguous subarrays so that the largest subarray sum is as small as possible, and return that minimized largest sum.

challenges.title: Minimum days to make bouquets
challenges.prompt: Write `minDays(bloomDay, m, k)`. Flower i blooms on day `bloomDay[i]`. A bouquet uses `k` adjacent bloomed flowers; you need `m` bouquets. Return the minimum number of days to wait, or `-1` if it is impossible.

challenges.title: Maximum profit job scheduling
challenges.prompt: Write `maxProfitJobs(jobs)` where `jobs[i] = [start, end, profit]`. Choose a subset of non-overlapping jobs (a job ending exactly when another starts is allowed) to maximize total profit. Return the maximum profit.

challenges.title: Polygon area ×2 (shoelace)
challenges.prompt: Given `pts`, the vertices of a simple polygon in order (either clockwise or counter-clockwise) as `[x,y]` integer pairs, return TWICE the polygon's area (an integer, always non-negative). Use the shoelace formula. The winding direction must NOT affect the result.

challenges.title: Point in polygon (boundary counts as inside)
challenges.prompt: Given a simple polygon `poly` (array of `[x,y]` integer vertices in order) and a query point `p=[x,y]`, return `true` if `p` is inside the polygon OR anywhere on its boundary (edges and vertices count as inside), else `false`.

challenges.title: Convex hull vertex count
challenges.prompt: Given a set of integer points `pts` (possibly with duplicates), return the number of vertices of their convex hull. Points that lie strictly ON a hull edge (collinear, not a corner) do NOT count. If all distinct points are collinear return 2; for one distinct point return 1; for empty input return 0.

challenges.title: Do two segments intersect (boolean)
challenges.prompt: Given two segments `s1=[[ax,ay],[bx,by]]` and `s2=[[cx,cy],[dx,dy]]` with integer endpoints, return `true` if they intersect in at least one point. This INCLUDES touching at an endpoint and collinear overlap (sharing any sub-segment or a single point). Return `false` only if they are fully disjoint.

challenges.title: Closest pair (squared distance)
challenges.prompt: Given `pts` (at least 2 integer points, possibly duplicated), return the SQUARED Euclidean distance of the closest pair of distinct indices. If two points coincide the answer is 0.

challenges.title: Max points on a line
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts` (duplicates allowed), return the maximum number of points that lie on a single straight line. Duplicate points count toward any line passing through that location. For 0 or 1 points return the count itself.

challenges.title: Is convex polygon (boolean)
challenges.prompt: Given `poly`, a simple polygon's vertices in order (`[x,y]` integers, no self-intersection), return `true` if it is convex, else `false`. Collinear consecutive vertices (a straight 180° angle) are allowed and keep the polygon convex. Fewer than 3 vertices are not a polygon: return `false`.

challenges.title: Interior lattice points (Pick's theorem)
challenges.prompt: Given a simple polygon `poly` with integer vertices, return the number of lattice points strictly INSIDE it (not on the boundary). Use Pick's theorem: Area = I + B/2 - 1, where B is the number of lattice points on the boundary (an edge from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) contains gcd(|dx|,|dy|) lattice steps).

challenges.title: Rectangle overlap area
challenges.prompt: Given two axis-aligned rectangles `a` and `b`, each as `[x1,y1,x2,y2]` with x1<x2 and y1<y2 (lower-left and upper-right corners, integers), return the area of their overlap. If they do not overlap, or only touch along an edge/corner (zero-area intersection), return 0.

challenges.title: Count intersecting segment pairs
challenges.prompt: Given `segs`, an array of segments each `[[x1,y1],[x2,y2]]` (integers), return the number of unordered pairs (i<j) of segments that intersect. Intersection INCLUDES touching at an endpoint and collinear overlap.

challenges.title: Minimum-area rectangle from 4 points
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts`, consider every rectangle whose 4 corners are all present in `pts` (the rectangle may be axis-aligned OR rotated). Return the smallest POSITIVE area among such rectangles, as an integer. If no rectangle can be formed, return 0.

challenges.title: Largest triangle area ×2
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts` (at least 3), return TWICE the maximum area of any triangle formed by three of the points (an integer, always non-negative). If all points are collinear the answer is 0.

challenges.title: Boundary lattice points of a polygon
challenges.prompt: Given a simple polygon `poly` with integer vertices, return the total number of lattice points lying ON its boundary. An edge from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) contributes gcd(|x2-x1|,|y2-y1|) points as you traverse it, so the total over all edges (each vertex counted once) is that sum.

challenges.title: Point strictly inside triangle
challenges.prompt: Given triangle vertices `a`, `b`, `c` and a point `p` (all `[x,y]` integers), return `true` if `p` lies STRICTLY inside the triangle. Points on any edge or vertex are NOT strictly inside (return `false`). A degenerate (zero-area) triangle has no interior: return `false`.

challenges.title: Convex hull area ×2
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts` in ARBITRARY order, return TWICE the area of their convex hull (an integer). If fewer than 3 distinct points, or all points are collinear, return 0.

challenges.title: Point on segment (boolean)
challenges.prompt: Given a segment's endpoints `a`, `b` and a point `p` (all `[x,y]` integers), return `true` if `p` lies on the segment `ab`, including its endpoints. The point must be BOTH collinear with a,b AND within the segment's bounding box.

challenges.title: Count collinear triples
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts` (duplicates allowed), return the number of unordered triples of indices (i<j<k) that are collinear. A triple is collinear if the three points lie on one line; any triple containing two coincident points is also collinear.

challenges.title: Rectangles strictly overlap (boolean)
challenges.prompt: Given two axis-aligned rectangles `a` and `b`, each `[x1,y1,x2,y2]` with x1<x2, y1<y2 (integers), return `true` if their intersection has POSITIVE area. Rectangles that merely touch along an edge or corner (zero-area intersection) do NOT count as overlapping.

challenges.title: Farthest pair (squared distance)
challenges.prompt: Given `pts` (at least 2 integer points), return the SQUARED Euclidean distance of the farthest pair of points (the squared diameter of the set).

challenges.title: Count non-degenerate triangles
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts` (duplicates allowed), return the number of unordered triples (i<j<k) that form a triangle with POSITIVE area (i.e. the three points are NOT collinear).

challenges.title: Point in convex polygon (any winding)
challenges.prompt: Given a convex polygon `poly` (vertices in order, either clockwise OR counter-clockwise, `[x,y]` integers) and a point `p`, return `true` if `p` is inside or on the boundary of the polygon. The winding direction of the input must NOT change the answer.

challenges.title: Lattice points strictly on a segment
challenges.prompt: Given a segment's endpoints `a` and `b` (`[x,y]` integers), return the number of lattice points strictly BETWEEN them (excluding both endpoints). This equals gcd(|dx|,|dy|) - 1, and is 0 when a and b coincide.

challenges.title: Largest axis-aligned rectangle from points
challenges.prompt: Given integer points `pts`, find the axis-aligned rectangle of largest area whose FOUR corners are ALL present in `pts`. Return that area as an integer, or 0 if no such rectangle exists.

challenges.title: Count points inside or on circle
challenges.prompt: Given integer center `cx,cy`, integer radius `r`, and integer points `pts`, return how many points lie inside OR exactly on the circle (i.e. squared distance to the center is <= r²).

challenges.title: Polygon orientation (signed area sign)
challenges.prompt: Given a simple polygon `poly` (vertices in order, `[x,y]` integers, possibly non-convex), return 1 if the vertices are ordered counter-clockwise, -1 if clockwise, and 0 if the polygon is degenerate (zero signed area). Use the sign of the FULL shoelace sum over all edges — a single vertex's turn is not enough for non-convex polygons.

challenges.title: Shortest path length (unweighted)
challenges.prompt: Given an adjacency list `adj` (adj[i] is an array of neighbors of node i) of a directed graph, and nodes `src` and `dst`, return the length (number of edges) of the SHORTEST path from src to dst, or -1 if dst is unreachable. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Number of islands (4-connected)
challenges.prompt: Given a 2D grid of 0s (water) and 1s (land), return the number of islands. An island is a group of 1s connected 4-directionally (up/down/left/right). Diagonal touches do NOT connect. Return 0 for an empty grid.

challenges.title: Connected components count
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list ([u,v] pairs), return the number of connected components. Isolated nodes count as their own component.

challenges.title: Detect cycle (directed)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and a directed `edges` list ([u,v] means edge u->v), return true if the graph contains a directed cycle, else false.

challenges.title: Detect cycle (undirected)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list ([u,v] pairs, no self-loops or duplicate edges), return true if the graph contains a cycle, else false.

challenges.title: Lexicographically smallest topological order
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and directed `edges` ([u,v] means u before v), return the LEXICOGRAPHICALLY SMALLEST valid topological ordering as an array. If no valid ordering exists (cycle), return []. At each step, among all nodes with no remaining incoming edges, pick the smallest-numbered one.

challenges.title: Bipartite check
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list, return true if the graph is bipartite (2-colorable so no edge joins same-color nodes), else false. The graph may be disconnected.

challenges.title: Word ladder length
challenges.prompt: Given `begin`, `end`, and a `words` list (all equal-length lowercase strings), return the number of words in the SHORTEST transformation sequence from begin to end, where each step changes exactly one letter and every intermediate word (and end) must be in `words`. Count both endpoints. Return 0 if no such sequence exists. `begin` need not be in `words`.

challenges.title: Weighted shortest path (Dijkstra)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1, an undirected weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w] with w>0), and nodes `src`/`dst`, return the minimum total weight of a path from src to dst, or -1 if unreachable. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Grid shortest path with obstacles (4-dir)
challenges.prompt: Given a grid where 0 is open and 1 is an obstacle, return the fewest number of CELLS on a path from the top-left (0,0) to the bottom-right (R-1,C-1), moving only up/down/left/right through open cells (count both endpoints). Return -1 if no path exists (including when start or end is an obstacle).

challenges.title: Tree diameter
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 forming a tree with undirected `edges` (exactly n-1 edges, connected), return the diameter: the number of EDGES on the longest path between any two nodes. For a single node return 0.

challenges.title: Flood fill (cells changed)
challenges.prompt: Given a 2D `grid` of integer colors, a start cell (`sr`,`sc`), and a `newColor`, perform a 4-directional flood fill of the region of cells sharing the start cell's original color, recoloring them to newColor. Return the NUMBER of cells whose color changed. If newColor equals the start cell's original color, nothing changes and you must return 0.

challenges.title: Course schedule (can finish)
challenges.prompt: There are `n` courses labeled 0..n-1. `prereqs` is a list of pairs [a,b] meaning you must take b before a. Return true if you can finish all courses (the prerequisite graph has no cycle), else false.

challenges.title: Number of provinces
challenges.prompt: Given an n×n symmetric adjacency `matrix` where matrix[i][j] = 1 means cities i and j are directly connected (matrix[i][i] = 1), return the number of provinces (connected groups of cities).

challenges.title: Max island area (4-connected)
challenges.prompt: Given a grid of 0s and 1s, return the maximum area (number of cells) of any island, where an island is a group of 1s connected 4-directionally. Return 0 if there is no land.

challenges.title: Count distinct paths in a DAG
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and directed `edges` forming a DAG, plus `src` and `dst`, return the number of distinct directed paths from src to dst. Return 1 if src === dst. Answers fit in a 32-bit integer.

challenges.title: Reachable node count (directed)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1, a DIRECTED `edges` list ([u,v] means u->v), and a start node `src`, return the number of nodes reachable from src, INCLUDING src itself.

challenges.title: Island perimeter
challenges.prompt: Given a grid of 0s (water) and 1s (land), return the total perimeter of all land cells. Each land cell contributes 4 minus the number of its 4-directional land neighbors. Cells on the grid edge contribute to the perimeter on their outward sides.

challenges.title: Shortest path in binary matrix (8-dir)
challenges.prompt: Given an n×n `grid` of 0s (clear) and 1s (blocked), return the length of the shortest clear path from top-left (0,0) to bottom-right (n-1,n-1), where you may move in all 8 directions between clear cells. Path length is the number of visited cells. Return -1 if there is no clear path (including when start or end is blocked).

challenges.title: Minimum knight moves on N×N board
challenges.prompt: On an N×N board with cells (row,col) for 0<=row,col<N, a knight starts at (sr,sc). Return the minimum number of knight moves to reach (tr,tc), or -1 if unreachable. A knight moves in the usual 8 L-shaped ways but may never leave the board.

challenges.title: Max depth of a rooted tree
challenges.prompt: Given a `parent` array where parent[i] is the parent of node i and the root has parent -1 (exactly one root; nodes are NOT guaranteed to be in any order relative to their parents), return the maximum depth measured in NUMBER OF NODES on the longest root-to-leaf path (a single-node tree has depth 1).

challenges.title: Longest path in a DAG
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and directed `edges` forming a DAG, return the number of EDGES on the longest directed path anywhere in the graph. Return 0 if there are no edges.

challenges.title: Valid tree
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list, return true if the edges form a valid tree: exactly one connected component AND no cycle (equivalently, connected with exactly n-1 edges). Return true for n=1 with no edges.

challenges.title: Count closed islands
challenges.prompt: Given a grid where 1 is land and 0 is water, return the number of CLOSED islands — islands of 1s (connected 4-directionally) that do NOT touch any border of the grid. Islands touching the top/bottom/left/right edge are not closed.

challenges.title: Rotting oranges
challenges.prompt: Given a grid where 0 is empty, 1 is a fresh orange, and 2 is a rotten orange, each minute every fresh orange 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten one becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if some fresh orange can never rot. Return 0 if there are no fresh oranges.

challenges.title: Pacific–Atlantic water flow (count)
challenges.prompt: Given an m×n `heights` grid, water can flow from a cell to an adjacent (4-directional) cell of EQUAL OR LOWER height. The Pacific ocean touches the top and left edges; the Atlantic touches the bottom and right edges. Return the number of cells from which water can reach BOTH oceans.

challenges.title: Number of enclaves
challenges.prompt: Given a grid of 0s (sea) and 1s (land), return the number of land cells from which it is IMPOSSIBLE to walk off the boundary of the grid, moving 4-directionally through land only. (Land connected to the border can escape.)

challenges.title: Keys and rooms
challenges.prompt: There are `n` rooms labeled 0..n-1. `rooms[i]` is a list of keys (room labels) found in room i. You start in room 0 (unlocked). Return true if you can visit ALL rooms, else false.

challenges.title: Redundant connection
challenges.prompt: An undirected graph started as a tree with n nodes (labeled 1..n) and had one extra edge added. Given the `edges` list in the order they were added, return the edge [u,v] that can be removed so the result is a tree. If multiple answers, return the edge that appears LAST in the input. Return it as a two-element array [u,v] in the same order it appears in the input.

challenges.title: Reorder routes to reach city 0
challenges.prompt: There are `n` cities 0..n-1 connected by n-1 directed roads `connections` ([a,b] is a road a->b) forming a tree if directions are ignored. Return the minimum number of roads that must be reversed so that EVERY city can reach city 0.

challenges.title: Shortest cycle length (girth)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list (no self-loops or duplicate edges), return the length (number of edges) of the SHORTEST cycle in the graph, or -1 if the graph is acyclic. The graph may be disconnected.

challenges.title: Unique paths with obstacles
challenges.prompt: Given a grid where 0 is free and 1 is an obstacle, return the number of distinct paths from the top-left to the bottom-right moving only RIGHT or DOWN through free cells. Return 0 if the start or end cell is an obstacle. Answers fit in a 32-bit integer.

challenges.title: Largest connected component size
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list, return the number of nodes in the LARGEST connected component. Isolated nodes are components of size 1.

challenges.title: Eventual safe nodes
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and directed `edges`, a node is SAFE if every possible path starting from it eventually reaches a terminal node (a node with no outgoing edges) — i.e. it can never enter a cycle. Return the sorted array of all safe nodes.

challenges.title: Network delay time
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 1..n and a directed weighted `times` list ([u,v,w] means a signal from u reaches v after w time, w>0), a signal starts at node `k`. Return the time it takes for ALL nodes to receive the signal (the maximum shortest-path distance from k), or -1 if some node is unreachable.

challenges.title: Min cost to connect points (MST)
challenges.prompt: Given `points` (array of [x,y]), the cost to connect two points is the Manhattan distance |x1-x2|+|y1-y2|. Return the minimum total cost to connect ALL points so every point is reachable from every other (a minimum spanning tree). Return 0 for 0 or 1 points.

challenges.title: Find the town judge
challenges.prompt: In a town of `n` people labeled 1..n, `trust` is a list of pairs [a,b] meaning a trusts b. The town judge trusts NOBODY, is trusted by EVERYONE else (n-1 people), and there is at most one. Return the judge's label, or -1 if there is no judge.

challenges.title: Count servers that communicate
challenges.prompt: Given a grid where 1 marks a server and 0 is empty, two servers communicate if they are on the same row or the same column. Return the number of servers that can communicate with AT LEAST one other server.

challenges.title: Distance to nearest zero (01 matrix)
challenges.prompt: Given a `mat` of 0s and 1s, return a matrix of the same shape where each cell holds the distance to the NEAREST 0 (4-directional steps). A 0 cell has distance 0. There is at least one 0 in the matrix.

challenges.title: Shortest path with obstacle elimination
challenges.prompt: Given a grid of 0s (free) and 1s (obstacles) and an integer `k`, return the minimum number of STEPS (moves between adjacent cells, 4-directional) to travel from the top-left to the bottom-right, where you may remove up to `k` obstacles along the way. Return -1 if impossible. The number of steps equals cells visited minus one.

challenges.title: Cheapest flights within K stops
challenges.prompt: Given `n` cities 0..n-1, a directed weighted `flights` list ([u,v,price]), a `src`, a `dst`, and an integer `k`, return the cheapest total price to fly from src to dst using AT MOST k intermediate stops (so at most k+1 flights), or -1 if impossible. Return 0 if src === dst.

challenges.title: Flood fill (return grid)
challenges.prompt: Given a 2D `grid` of integer colors, a start cell (`sr`,`sc`), and a `newColor`, flood fill the 4-connected region sharing the start cell's color, recoloring it to newColor, and return the resulting grid. If newColor equals the start color, return the grid unchanged.

challenges.title: As far from land as possible
challenges.prompt: Given an n×n `grid` of 0s (water) and 1s (land), return the LARGEST Manhattan distance from any WATER cell to its nearest land cell (4-directional). If the grid has no water or no land, return -1.

challenges.title: Shortest path visiting all nodes
challenges.prompt: Given an undirected connected graph as an adjacency list `adj` (adj[i] is the list of neighbors of node i), return the length (number of edges) of the shortest walk that visits EVERY node at least once. You may start and end at any node and revisit nodes and edges. There are at most 10 nodes.

challenges.title: Weighted graph diameter (all-pairs)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected weighted `edges` list ([u,v,w], w>0, possibly multiple edges — take the minimum), return the graph's DIAMETER: the maximum over all pairs of the shortest-path distance between them. If the graph is disconnected (some pair unreachable) return -1. Return 0 for n <= 1.

challenges.title: Nim (who wins)
challenges.prompt: Two players play standard Nim on `piles` (array of non-negative pile sizes). On a turn a player removes any positive number of stones from a single pile. The player who takes the last stone wins (normal play). Write `nimWin(piles)` returning true if the player to move first can force a win with optimal play.

challenges.title: Misère Nim
challenges.prompt: Two players play Misère Nim on `piles` (each pile >= 1, at least one pile). A turn removes any positive number of stones from one pile. The player who takes the LAST stone LOSES. Write `misereNimWin(piles)` returning true if the first player can force a win with optimal play.

challenges.title: Composite subtraction game (Grundy value)
challenges.prompt: A composite game has independent piles. From a single pile you may remove exactly `m` stones for any `m` in the sorted array `moves` (m <= current pile size).
