Last player to move wins. Write `subtractionGrundy(piles, moves)` returning the Grundy value of the whole position: the XOR of the Grundy numbers of the individual piles. (Grundy(size) is the mex of the Grundy values of reachable sizes.)

challenges.title: Bachet's take-away game
challenges.prompt: A single pile has `n` stones. On a turn a player removes between 1 and `k` stones (inclusive). The player who takes the last stone wins. Write `bachetGameWin(n, k)` returning true if the first player can force a win with optimal play.

challenges.title: Subtraction-set game (single pile)
challenges.prompt: A single pile has `n` stones. On a turn a player removes exactly `m` stones for some `m` in the array `moves` (m <= current size). The player who cannot move (leaves an empty pile with no legal move) loses; equivalently the last player to move wins. Write `subtractionSetWin(n, moves)` returning true if the first player can force a win.

challenges.title: Divisor game
challenges.prompt: The number `n` (n >= 1) is on a board. On a turn a player chooses an `x` with 0 < x < n and n % x === 0, then replaces n with n - x. A player who cannot move (n === 1) loses. Write `divisorGameWin(n)` returning true if the first player can force a win with optimal play.

challenges.title: Flip game II (can win)
challenges.prompt: The string `s` consists of '+' and '-'. On a turn a player chooses two consecutive '+' characters ("++") and flips them to "--". A player who cannot move loses. Write `flipGameCanWin(s)` returning true if the player to move first can guarantee a win with optimal play.

challenges.title: Predict the winner
challenges.prompt: Given an array `nums` of non-negative scores, two players alternately take a value from either the front or the back of the array, adding it to their own total. Player 1 goes first; both play optimally to maximize their own total. Write `predictTheWinner(nums)` returning true if player 1's final total is >= player 2's (i.e. player 1 does not lose).

challenges.title: Coins in a line (optimal value)
challenges.prompt: `coins` is a row of coin values. Two players alternately take a coin from either end; player 1 goes first and both play optimally to maximize the total value they collect. Write `coinsInLineValue(coins)` returning the total value player 1 collects under optimal play by both.

challenges.title: Stone game (score difference)
challenges.prompt: `piles` is a row of stone counts. Two players alternately take a whole pile from either end and add its stones to their score; player 1 first, both optimal. Write `stoneGameDiff(piles)` returning player 1's score minus player 2's score under optimal play by both.

challenges.title: Stone game III (First/Second/Tie)
challenges.prompt: `values` is a row of stone values (may be negative). Players alternate; on a turn a player takes the first 1, 2, or 3 remaining stones from the front, scoring their sum. Player 1 ("First") goes first, both play optimally to maximize their own score. Write `stoneGameIII(values)` returning "First", "Second", or "Tie" for who ends with the higher total (or a tie).

challenges.title: Stone game II (piles and M)
challenges.prompt: `piles` holds stone counts. Players alternate; M starts at 1. On a turn a player takes ALL stones from the first X remaining piles, where 1 <= X <= 2*M, then M becomes max(M, X). Both maximize their own total. Write `stoneGameII(piles)` returning the maximum number of stones the first player can secure with optimal play.

challenges.title: Can I win
challenges.prompt: Two players draw from the integer pool 1..maxChoosable (each integer usable once) and add to a shared running total. A player who makes the running total reach or exceed `desiredTotal` on their move wins. Write `canIWin(maxChoosable, desiredTotal)` returning true if the first player can force a win. If desiredTotal <= 0 the first player wins immediately; if the whole pool can't reach desiredTotal, return false.

challenges.title: Guess number (min worst-case cost)
challenges.prompt: You pick a secret integer in 1..n. On each guess g you are told whether the secret is higher, lower, or equal; a wrong guess of g costs g dollars. Write `guessNumberMinCost(n)` returning the minimum amount of money that guarantees a win regardless of the secret (optimal strategy against a worst-case secret).

challenges.title: Minimax on a game tree
challenges.prompt: A two-player game tree is given as nested arrays. A leaf is a number (its value). An internal node is a non-empty array of child nodes. The root is a MAX node; levels then alternate MIN, MAX, MIN, ... Write `minimaxTree(tree)` returning the minimax value of the root (each player plays optimally: MAX maximizes, MIN minimizes).

challenges.title: Stone game (does first strictly win)
challenges.prompt: `piles` is a row of positive stone counts. Two players alternately take a whole pile from either end, adding its stones to their score (player 1 first, both optimal). Write `stoneGameClassicWin(piles)` returning true only if player 1's final score is STRICTLY greater than player 2's.

challenges.title: Cat and mouse (small graph)
challenges.prompt: `graph` is an adjacency list: graph[i] lists the neighbors of node i. A Mouse starts at node 1 and moves first; a Cat starts at node 2. They alternate moving along an edge to an adjacent node. The Cat may not move to the Hole (node 0). The Mouse wins if it reaches node 0; the Cat wins if it occupies the same node as the Mouse; if the game could continue forever with optimal play it is a Draw. Write `catMouseLite(graph)` returning 1 (Mouse wins), 2 (Cat wins), or 0 (Draw), assuming optimal play.

challenges.title: Stone game VII (remaining-sum diff)
challenges.prompt: `stones` is a row of values. Players alternate; on a turn a player removes the leftmost or rightmost stone and scores the SUM of the stones that remain after removal. Player 1 first, both maximize their own score. Write `stoneGameVII(stones)` returning player 1's score minus player 2's score under optimal play.

challenges.title: Bounded subtraction Nim (composite)
challenges.prompt: There are several piles. On a turn a player removes between 1 and `k` stones (inclusive) from a single pile. Last player to move wins. Write `boundedNimComposite(piles, k)` returning true if the first player can force a win. (Each pile's Grundy value is size mod (k+1); XOR them.)

challenges.title: Predict the winner (score diff)
challenges.prompt: Given array `nums`, two players alternately take a value from either end (player 1 first, both optimal to maximize their own total). Write `predictWinnerDiff(nums)` returning player 1's total minus player 2's total under optimal play by both.

challenges.title: Square-removal game
challenges.prompt: A pile has `n` stones. On a turn a player removes a positive perfect-square number of stones (1, 4, 9, 16, ...). The player who cannot move (n === 0 on their turn) loses. Write `squareGameWin(n)` returning true if the first player can force a win with optimal play.

challenges.title: Bounded Nim Grundy value
challenges.prompt: There are several piles. On a turn a player removes between 1 and `k` stones from a single pile; last to move wins. Write `boundedNimGrundy(piles, k)` returning the Grundy value of the whole position: the XOR over piles of (pile size mod (k+1)).

challenges.title: Minimax with chosen starting player
challenges.prompt: A game tree is given as nested arrays (leaf = number, internal node = non-empty array of children). `maxStarts` is a boolean for whether the root node is a MAX node (true) or a MIN node (false); levels alternate below the root. Write `minimaxRoot(tree, maxStarts)` returning the minimax value of the root.

challenges.title: Staircase Nim
challenges.prompt: Steps are numbered 1..n from the array `steps` (steps[i] stones on step i+1). On a turn a player moves any positive number of stones from a step down to the next-lower step; stones moved off step 1 leave the board. A player who cannot move loses. The outcome is decided by Nim on the ODD-numbered steps. Write `staircaseNimWin(steps)` returning true if the first player can force a win — i.e. the XOR of the stone counts on the odd-numbered steps (steps 1, 3, 5, ... which are indices 0, 2, 4, ...) is non-zero.

challenges.title: Minimax on a labeled (non-alternating) tree
challenges.prompt: A game tree is given where a leaf is a number and an internal node is an object {"p": 0 or 1, "c": [children...]}. p=0 means the node is a MAX node, p=1 means a MIN node. Players do NOT necessarily alternate — each internal node's own label determines whether it maximizes or minimizes over its children's values. Write `minimaxLabeled(tree)` returning the value of the root.

challenges.title: Search in rotated sorted array
challenges.prompt: An ascending array of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown pivot. Write `searchRotated(nums, target)` returning the index of `target`, or -1 if it is absent. Run in O(log n).

challenges.title: Find a peak element
challenges.prompt: Write `findPeak(nums)` returning the index of a peak: an element strictly greater than its neighbors. Out-of-bounds neighbors count as -Infinity, so ends can be peaks. The array is non-empty and no two adjacent elements are equal. Return any valid peak index; run in O(log n). For determinism, when the classic O(log n) binary search applies, return the index it converges to.

challenges.title: Koko eating bananas
challenges.prompt: Given piles[] of bananas and an integer h hours, Koko eats at some integer speed k bananas/hour; each hour she picks one pile and eats up to k from it (finishing a pile early wastes the rest of that hour). Write `minEatingSpeed(piles, h)` returning the minimum integer k so she finishes all piles within h hours. Guaranteed h >= piles.length.

challenges.title: Split array — minimize largest sum
challenges.prompt: Write `splitArray(nums, k)` splitting nums (non-negative integers) into k non-empty contiguous subarrays so the largest subarray sum is minimized; return that minimized largest sum. 1 <= k <= nums.length.

challenges.title: Ship packages within D days
challenges.prompt: weights[] are loaded onto a ship in the given order. Each day the ship carries a prefix of the remaining weights whose sum does not exceed its capacity. Write `shipWithinDays(weights, days)` returning the least capacity that ships everything within `days` days.

challenges.title: Median of two sorted arrays
challenges.prompt: Write `findMedian(a, b)` returning the median of the two sorted arrays combined, as a number. If the combined length is even, return the average of the two middle values (may be a .5 fraction). Run in O(log(min(m,n))).

challenges.title: Integer square root
challenges.prompt: Write `isqrt(x)` returning floor(sqrt(x)) for a non-negative integer x, using only integer arithmetic (no Math.sqrt). 0 <= x <= 2^53-1.

challenges.title: Integer nth root
challenges.prompt: Write `nthRoot(x, n)` returning floor(x^(1/n)) for integers x >= 0 and n >= 1, using integer arithmetic only (no Math.pow/Math.sqrt with fractional exponents). Answer fits in a 32-bit range.

challenges.title: Kth smallest in a sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: Given an n x n matrix where each row and each column is sorted ascending, write `kthSmallest(matrix, k)` returning the k-th smallest element (1-indexed) in the whole matrix. Duplicates count by position.

challenges.title: Aggressive cows (maximize min distance)
challenges.prompt: Given stall positions[] (unsorted) and an integer c cows, place the cows in distinct stalls so the minimum distance between any two cows is as large as possible. Write `maxMinDist(positions, c)` returning that largest possible minimum distance. 2 <= c <= positions.length.

challenges.title: First and last position of a value
challenges.prompt: Write `searchRange(nums, target)` returning [firstIndex, lastIndex] of `target` in the ascending (possibly duplicated) array, or [-1,-1] if absent.

challenges.title: Minimum in rotated sorted array
challenges.prompt: An ascending array of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown pivot. Write `findMin(nums)` returning the minimum element in O(log n).

challenges.title: Search rotated array with duplicates
challenges.prompt: An ascending array (may contain duplicates) was rotated at an unknown pivot. Write `existsRotated(nums, target)` returning true if target is present, else false.

challenges.title: Smallest divisor given a threshold
challenges.prompt: Write `smallestDivisor(nums, threshold)` returning the smallest positive integer d such that the sum over nums of ceil(num/d) is <= threshold. Guaranteed threshold >= nums.length.

challenges.title: Place stations to minimize max gap
challenges.prompt: Sorted integer positions stations[] lie on a line, and you may add k extra stations at any integer positions. Write `minMaxGap(stations, k)` returning the smallest integer D achievable as the largest gap between adjacent stations. Covering a gap of length g so every piece is <= D costs ceil(g/D)-1 added stations, and the total added must not exceed k.

challenges.title: Insertion index (lower bound)
challenges.prompt: Write `searchInsert(nums, target)` returning the index where target is, or where it would be inserted to keep the ascending array sorted (the number of elements strictly less than target).

challenges.title: K closest elements
challenges.prompt: Given an ascending array arr, an integer k, and a value x, write `kClosest(arr, k, x)` returning the k elements closest to x, as an ascending subarray. Closeness ties break toward the smaller value.

challenges.title: Peak index in a mountain array
challenges.prompt: arr strictly increases then strictly decreases (a mountain, length >= 3). Write `peakIndexMountain(arr)` returning the index of the maximum, in O(log n).

challenges.title: Max side of square (search on answer)
challenges.prompt: You have `bricks` unit bricks. A solid square of side s needs s*s bricks; a border frame of side s (outline only, 1 brick thick) needs 4*s-4 bricks for s>=2 and 1 brick for s=1. Write `maxSquareSide(bricks, solid)` returning the largest side s buildable given `bricks`, where `solid` is a boolean choosing solid (true) or frame (false). bricks >= 1.

challenges.title: Count values within an inclusive range
challenges.prompt: Given an ascending array nums and integers lo and hi (lo <= hi), write `countInRange(nums, lo, hi)` returning how many elements x satisfy lo <= x <= hi. Use binary search; O(log n).

challenges.title: Minimum time to complete trips
challenges.prompt: Buses have times[] (time for one trip each). All buses run in parallel and repeat continuously. Write `minimumTime(times, totalTrips)` returning the least time T at which the combined number of completed trips (sum of floor(T/t)) reaches totalTrips.

challenges.title: Rotation count of a sorted array
challenges.prompt: An ascending array of distinct integers was rotated right by some amount r (0 <= r < n). Write `rotationCount(nums)` returning r, which equals the index of the minimum element. O(log n).

challenges.title: Allocate minimum number of pages
challenges.prompt: books[] are page counts in a fixed order; assign contiguous blocks of books to s students so each student gets >=1 book. Write `allocatePages(books, s)` minimizing the maximum pages any student reads; return that minimum. If s > books.length return -1.

challenges.title: Kth smallest pair distance
challenges.prompt: Write `smallestDistancePair(nums, k)` returning the k-th smallest absolute difference |nums[i]-nums[j]| over all pairs i<j (1-indexed k).

challenges.title: Single element in a sorted pairs array
challenges.prompt: In an ascending array every value appears exactly twice except one value that appears once. Write `singleNonDuplicate(nums)` returning that single value in O(log n). Length is always odd.

challenges.title: Maximum minimum magnetic force
challenges.prompt: positions[] (unsorted) are basket locations. Place m balls in distinct baskets to maximize the minimum pairwise distance (the 'force'). Write `maxForce(positions, m)` returning that maximum minimum distance. 2 <= m <= positions.length.

challenges.title: Median of a row-wise sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: A matrix has R rows and C columns (R*C is odd); each row is sorted ascending. Write `matrixMedian(matrix)` returning the median value (the ((R*C+1)/2)-th smallest) using binary search on value + per-row upper-bound counting.

challenges.title: Minimum days for m bouquets
challenges.prompt: bloomDay[] gives the day each flower blooms. To make a bouquet you need k adjacent flowers all bloomed. Write `minDays(bloomDay, m, k)` returning the least day to make m bouquets, or -1 if impossible (m*k > flowers).

challenges.title: Successful spell-potion pairs
challenges.prompt: spells[] and potions[] are positive integers. For each spell, a potion is a success if spell*potion >= success. Write `successfulPairs(spells, potions, success)` returning an array where entry i is the count of potions succeeding with spells[i]. Sort potions and binary-search each query.

challenges.title: Minimum speed to arrive on time
challenges.prompt: dist[] are leg distances of a train journey; each leg after boarding waits for an integer departure, so the time for all legs except the last is ceil(dist[i]/speed), and the last leg is dist[last]/speed exactly. Write `minSpeedOnTime(dist, hour)` returning the least integer speed to arrive within `hour` (a number that may have up to two decimals), or -1 if impossible.

challenges.title: Spiral order traversal
challenges.prompt: Write `spiralOrder(matrix)` that returns all elements of the given matrix (array of rows) in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner. Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Counterclockwise spiral
challenges.prompt: Write `spiralCCW(matrix)` returning all elements in counterclockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner and moving DOWN first. Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Rotate image 90 clockwise
challenges.prompt: Write `rotate90(matrix)` returning a NEW matrix that is the input rotated 90 degrees clockwise. Works for any rectangular matrix (an R x C input becomes C x R).

challenges.title: Rotate image 90 counterclockwise
challenges.prompt: Write `rotate90ccw(matrix)` returning a NEW matrix that is the input rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise. Works for any rectangular matrix (an R x C input becomes C x R).

challenges.title: Rotate image 180
challenges.prompt: Write `rotate180(matrix)` returning a NEW matrix rotated 180 degrees (both rows and columns reversed). Works for any rectangular matrix.

challenges.title: Set matrix zeroes
challenges.prompt: Write `setZeroes(matrix)` that, for every cell originally equal to 0, sets that cell's entire row and column to 0. Base the zeroing on the ORIGINAL positions of the zeroes, then return the modified matrix.

challenges.title: Search a fully-sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `searchMatrix(matrix, target)` returning true if target is present. Each row is sorted ascending, and the first element of each row is greater than the last element of the previous row (so the matrix is fully sorted in row-major order).

challenges.title: Search a staircase-sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `searchMatrixII(matrix, target)` returning true if target is present. Each row is sorted left-to-right and each column is sorted top-to-bottom, but the matrix is NOT necessarily fully sorted in row-major order.

challenges.title: Max sum k x k submatrix
challenges.prompt: Write `maxKxK(matrix, k)` returning the maximum sum over all contiguous k x k submatrices. You may assume 1 <= k <= min(rows, cols).

challenges.title: Transpose matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `transpose(matrix)` returning a NEW matrix that is the transpose of the input (element at [r][c] moves to [c][r]). Works for any rectangular matrix.

challenges.title: Diagonal zigzag traverse
challenges.prompt: Write `diagonalTraverse(matrix)` returning all elements in diagonal zigzag order: the first diagonal goes up-right, the next goes down-left, alternating. (LeetCode 'Diagonal Traverse'.) Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Game of Life next step
challenges.prompt: Write `gameOfLife(board)` returning the NEXT state of a Conway's Game of Life grid (each cell 0 dead or 1 alive). A live cell survives with 2 or 3 live neighbors; a dead cell becomes alive with exactly 3 live neighbors. All 8 neighbors count; cells off the grid do not exist.

challenges.title: Robot bounded in circle
challenges.prompt: Write `isRobotBounded(instructions)`. A robot starts at the origin facing north and repeats the instruction string forever: 'G' moves one step forward, 'L' turns left 90 degrees, 'R' turns right 90 degrees. Return true if there exists a circle that the robot never leaves.

challenges.title: Count negatives in sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `countNegatives(grid)` returning the number of strictly-negative values. The grid is sorted in non-increasing order both row-wise (left to right) and column-wise (top to bottom).

challenges.title: Matrix diagonal sum
challenges.prompt: Write `diagonalSum(matrix)` for a SQUARE matrix, returning the sum of the two diagonals. If the matrix has odd dimension, the center element (shared by both diagonals) must be counted only once.

challenges.title: Boustrophedon row read
challenges.prompt: Write `snakeRead(matrix)` returning a flat array read in snake (boustrophedon) order by rows: row 0 left-to-right, row 1 right-to-left, row 2 left-to-right, and so on. Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Boustrophedon column read
challenges.prompt: Write `snakeCols(matrix)` returning a flat array read in snake (boustrophedon) order by columns: column 0 top-to-bottom, column 1 bottom-to-top, column 2 top-to-bottom, and so on. Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Flip and invert image
challenges.prompt: Write `flipAndInvert(image)` for a binary matrix: first reverse each row horizontally, then invert every value (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0). Return the resulting matrix.

challenges.title: Anti-diagonal order
challenges.prompt: Write `antiDiagonals(matrix)` returning a flat array of the anti-diagonals (cells where row+col is constant) in increasing order of row+col, and within each anti-diagonal ordered by increasing row index. Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Reshape the matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `reshape(matrix, r, c)` that reshapes the matrix into r rows and c columns, filling in row-major order. If the reshape is impossible (element counts differ), return the original matrix unchanged.

challenges.title: Generate spiral matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `spiralGenerate(rows, cols)` returning a rows x cols matrix filled with 1..rows*cols in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner and moving right.

challenges.title: Row with the most ones
challenges.prompt: Write `rowWithMaxOnes(matrix)` for a binary matrix, returning the index of the row containing the most 1s. If several rows tie, return the SMALLEST such index. Return -1 for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Submatrix region sum
challenges.prompt: Write `regionSum(matrix, r1, c1, r2, c2)` returning the sum of all elements in the rectangle whose top-left corner is (r1,c1) and bottom-right corner is (r2,c2), inclusive.

challenges.title: Kth smallest in sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `kthSmallest(matrix, k)` returning the k-th smallest element (1-indexed) of a matrix whose rows and columns are each sorted in ascending order. Note the matrix is NOT necessarily sorted in row-major order.

challenges.title: Toeplitz matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `isToeplitz(matrix)` returning true if the matrix is Toeplitz: every top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal has all equal values.

challenges.title: Matrix boundary traversal
challenges.prompt: Write `boundary(matrix)` returning the elements on the outer border in clockwise order, starting at the top-left corner: top row left-to-right, right column downward, bottom row right-to-left, left column upward. Do not repeat any cell. Return an empty array for an empty matrix.

challenges.title: Sort matrix diagonals
challenges.prompt: Write `diagonalSort(matrix)` returning a NEW matrix in which each top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal has been sorted in ascending order (values stay on their own diagonal).

challenges.title: Largest local 3x3 maxima
challenges.prompt: Write `maxLocal(grid)` for an n x n grid (n >= 3). Return the (n-2) x (n-2) matrix where each cell holds the maximum value of the surrounding 3 x 3 block in the original grid.

challenges.title: Diagonal difference
challenges.prompt: Write `diagonalDifference(matrix)` for a SQUARE matrix, returning the absolute value of (sum of the main diagonal) minus (sum of the anti-diagonal).

challenges.title: Rotate to match target
challenges.prompt: Write `findRotation(mat, target)` returning true if the square matrix `mat` can be rotated in place by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees (clockwise) so that it equals `target`.

challenges.title: Kth largest element
challenges.prompt: Write `kthLargest(nums, k)` returning the kth largest element of `nums` (1-indexed). Duplicates count as separate elements: in [3,3,2] the 1st largest is 3 and the 2nd largest is also 3.

challenges.title: Kth smallest element
challenges.prompt: Write `kthSmallest(nums, k)` returning the kth smallest element of `nums` (1-indexed, duplicates counted).

challenges.title: K closest points to origin
challenges.prompt: Write `kClosest(points, k)` returning the `k` points closest to the origin (Euclidean distance), as an array of [x,y]. Sort the result by distance ascending; break ties by smaller x, then smaller y.

challenges.title: Merge k sorted arrays
challenges.prompt: Write `mergeK(lists)` where `lists` is an array of ascending-sorted integer arrays. Return a single ascending-sorted array containing all elements (duplicates kept).

challenges.title: Top-k frequent numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `topKFrequent(nums, k)` returning the `k` most frequent values as an array. Order by frequency descending; break ties by smaller value first.

challenges.title: Running medians of a stream
challenges.prompt: Write `streamMedians(nums)` returning an array where element i is the median of nums[0..i] inclusive. For an even number of elements the median is the average of the two middle values (may be fractional).

challenges.title: Reorganize string feasibility
challenges.prompt: Write `canReorganize(s)` returning true if the characters of `s` can be rearranged so that no two adjacent characters are equal. The empty string returns true.

challenges.title: Last stone weight
challenges.prompt: Write `lastStoneWeight(stones)`. Repeatedly take the two heaviest stones x <= y and smash them: if x === y both vanish, else a new stone of weight y - x appears. Return the weight of the last remaining stone, or 0 if none remain.

challenges.title: Kth smallest in a sorted matrix
challenges.prompt: Write `kthSmallest(matrix, k)` where each row and each column of `matrix` is sorted ascending. Return the kth smallest element (1-indexed, duplicates counted) over all elements.

challenges.title: Minimize cost to connect sticks
challenges.prompt: Write `connectSticks(sticks)`. Repeatedly combine the two shortest sticks into one of length equal to their sum; the cost of each combine is that sum. Return the minimum total cost to combine all sticks into one. Zero or one stick costs 0.

challenges.title: Sliding window median
challenges.prompt: Write `windowMedians(nums, k)` returning the median of every contiguous window of size `k`, left to right. For even `k` the median is the average of the two middle values (may be fractional).

challenges.title: Task scheduler time
challenges.prompt: Write `leastInterval(tasks, n)` where `tasks` is an array of single-character task ids and `n` is the cooldown: two runs of the same task must be at least n intervals apart. Each interval runs one task or idles. Return the least number of intervals to finish all tasks.

challenges.title: Kth largest distinct value
challenges.prompt: Write `kthLargestDistinct(nums, k)` returning the kth largest DISTINCT value in `nums` (1-indexed), or -1 if there are fewer than k distinct values.

challenges.title: Sort characters by frequency
challenges.prompt: Write `frequencySort(s)` returning a string with the characters of `s` ordered by decreasing frequency. Characters with equal frequency are ordered by their character code ascending.

challenges.title: Sort array by frequency
challenges.prompt: Write `sortByFrequency(nums)` returning all elements sorted by frequency ascending. Elements with equal frequency are ordered by value descending.

challenges.title: K closest values to a target
challenges.prompt: Write `kClosest(arr, k, x)` where `arr` is sorted ascending. Return the `k` values closest to `x`, sorted ascending. If two values are equally close, prefer the smaller one.

challenges.title: Third distinct maximum
challenges.prompt: Write `thirdMax(nums)` returning the third distinct maximum value. If the third distinct maximum does not exist, return the maximum value.

challenges.title: K pairs with smallest sums
challenges.prompt: Write `kSmallestPairs(nums1, nums2, k)`. Form all pairs [a,b] with a from nums1 and b from nums2 (arrays are NOT necessarily sorted). Return the `k` pairs with the smallest sums, ordered by sum ascending, ties broken by smaller a then smaller b.

challenges.title: Minimum meeting rooms
challenges.prompt: Write `minMeetingRooms(intervals)` where each interval is [start, end] with start < end. Return the minimum number of rooms needed so no two overlapping meetings share a room. A meeting ending exactly when another starts does NOT conflict.

challenges.title: Nth ugly number
challenges.prompt: Write `nthUglyNumber(n)` returning the nth positive ugly number (1-indexed). Ugly numbers are positive integers whose only prime factors are 2, 3, or 5. By convention 1 is ugly. The sequence begins 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, ...

challenges.title: Top-k frequent words
challenges.prompt: Write `topKWords(words, k)` returning the `k` most frequent words as an array. Order by frequency descending; break ties alphabetically (ascending).

challenges.title: Median of two sorted arrays
challenges.prompt: Write `findMedian(a, b)` returning the median of the combined multiset of the two ascending-sorted arrays `a` and `b`. For an even total count the median is the average of the two middle values (may be fractional).

challenges.title: Smallest range covering k lists
challenges.prompt: Write `smallestRange(lists)` where `lists` is an array of ascending-sorted integer arrays. Return [start, end], the smallest range that includes at least one number from each list. If several ranges tie in size, return the one with the smaller start.

challenges.title: Median over a stream of ops
challenges.prompt: Write `medianOps(ops, vals)`. `ops[i]` is either 'add' (insert vals[i] into the multiset) or 'median' (query, vals[i] ignored). Return an array with the median produced by each 'median' op in order. For an even count the median is the average of the two middle values (may be fractional). A 'median' op is only issued when at least one element has been added.

challenges.title: H-index
challenges.prompt: Write `hIndex(citations)` where `citations[i]` is the citation count of the i-th paper. Return the h-index: the largest h such that at least h papers each have at least h citations.

challenges.title: Minimum set size to remove half
challenges.prompt: Write `minSetSize(arr)` returning the minimum number of distinct values you must remove (removing a value deletes all its occurrences) so that at least half of the array's elements are removed.

challenges.title: Rank teams by votes
challenges.prompt: Write `rankTeams(votes)` where each vote is a string ranking all teams (each character a team). Rank teams by number of first-place votes descending; break ties by second-place votes, then third-place, and so on; if still tied, break alphabetically ascending. Return the ranking as a string.

challenges.title: Maximum score with reductions
challenges.prompt: Write `maxScore(nums, k)`. Perform exactly `k` operations; each operation picks the current largest element x, adds x to the score, and replaces that element with ceil(x / 3). Return the maximum total score.

challenges.title: Largest number from arrangement
challenges.prompt: Write `largestNumber(nums)` where `nums` is an array of non-negative integers. Arrange them to form the largest possible number and return it as a string. If the result would be all zeros, return "0".

challenges.title: Reconstruct queue by height
challenges.prompt: Write `reconstructQueue(people)` where each entry is [h, k]: a person of height `h` with exactly `k` people of height >= h in front of them. Return the reconstructed queue as an array of [h, k].

challenges.title: Group anagrams (canonical)
challenges.prompt: Write `groupAnagrams(words)` that groups the strings into anagram classes. Return an array of groups: within each group the words are sorted ascending, and the groups themselves are sorted ascending by their first word.

challenges.title: Longest consecutive sequence
challenges.prompt: Write `longestConsecutive(nums)` returning the length of the longest run of consecutive integers found among the values (array order is irrelevant; duplicates count only once).

challenges.title: Subarray sum equals k
challenges.prompt: Write `subarraySum(nums, k)` returning the number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum exactly to k. Values may be negative or zero.

challenges.title: Top-k frequent (tie-break)
challenges.prompt: Write `topKFrequent(nums, k)` returning the k most frequent values, sorted by frequency descending, ties broken by value ascending.

challenges.title: First unique character
challenges.prompt: Write `firstUniqChar(s)` returning the index of the first character that occurs exactly once in s, or -1 if there is none.

challenges.title: Isomorphic strings
challenges.prompt: Write `isIsomorphic(s, t)` returning true iff the characters of s can be replaced to get t under a one-to-one (bijective) mapping. No two distinct characters may map to the same character.

challenges.title: LRU cache final state
challenges.prompt: Write `lruFinalState(capacity, ops)`. Each op is ["put", key, val] or ["get", key]. Simulate an LRU cache: both a put and a successful get mark a key most-recently-used, and a put that exceeds capacity evicts the least-recently-used key. Return the final contents as [key, val] pairs ordered most-recently-used first.

challenges.title: Design hit counter
challenges.prompt: Write `hitCounter(events)`. Each event is ["hit", t] or ["query", t] with t nondecreasing (seconds). A query returns how many hits happened in the most recent 300 seconds: hits with timestamp strictly greater than t-300 (the window is the 300 seconds up to and including t). Return the array of query results in order.

challenges.title: Most common (tie-break smallest)
challenges.prompt: Write `mostCommon(nums)` returning the most frequent value; if several values tie for most frequent, return the smallest of them.

challenges.title: Sliding window distinct counts
challenges.prompt: Write `distinctInWindows(nums, k)` returning, for every contiguous window of length k (left to right), the number of distinct values in that window. Assume 1 <= k <= nums.length.

challenges.title: Unique two-sum value pairs
challenges.prompt: Write `uniquePairs(nums, target)` returning all unique value pairs [a, b] with a <= b and a + b = target. A pair with a === b is valid only if that value occurs at least twice in nums. Sort pairs by a ascending then b ascending.

challenges.title: Find all anagram indices
challenges.prompt: Write `findAnagrams(s, p)` returning, in ascending order, all start indices i such that the length-|p| substring of s beginning at i is an anagram (same multiset of characters) of p.

challenges.title: Longest substring without repeat
challenges.prompt: Write `lengthOfLongestSubstring(s)` returning the length of the longest substring of s that contains no repeated character.

challenges.title: Palindrome permutation
challenges.prompt: Write `canPermutePalindrome(s)` returning true iff some permutation of s is a palindrome.

challenges.title: First duplicate value
challenges.prompt: Write `firstDuplicate(nums)` returning the value whose second occurrence appears earliest (the value at the smallest index that is a repeat of an earlier value). Return -1 if no value repeats.

challenges.title: Multiset intersection
challenges.prompt: Write `intersect(a, b)` returning the intersection of the two arrays as a multiset: each value appears min(count in a, count in b) times. Return the result sorted ascending.

challenges.title: Majority element or -1
challenges.prompt: Write `majorityElement(nums)` returning the value that appears strictly more than nums.length/2 times, or -1 if no such value exists.

challenges.title: Nearby duplicate within k
challenges.prompt: Write `containsNearbyDuplicate(nums, k)` returning true iff there exist two distinct indices i, j with nums[i] === nums[j] and |i - j| <= k.

challenges.title: Sort by frequency then value
challenges.prompt: Write `frequencySort(nums)` returning the array reordered so more frequent values come first; values with equal frequency are ordered by value ascending. Every element (with its multiplicity) appears in the output.

challenges.title: Unique email addresses
challenges.prompt: Write `numUniqueEmails(emails)` returning the number of distinct addresses after normalizing each: in the local part (before '@') drop everything from the first '+' onward and remove all '.' characters; the domain part is left unchanged.

challenges.title: Unique pairs with difference k
challenges.prompt: Write `countPairsWithDiff(nums, k)` (k >= 0) returning the number of unique unordered value pairs whose absolute difference is exactly k. When k === 0 this counts values that occur at least twice.

challenges.title: Most frequent even number
challenges.prompt: Write `mostFrequentEven(nums)` returning the most frequent even value; break ties by the smallest such value. Return -1 if there is no even value.

challenges.title: Elements appearing exactly twice
challenges.prompt: Write `elementsTwice(nums)` returning, sorted ascending, the values that appear exactly two times in nums.

challenges.title: Longest palindrome from letters
challenges.prompt: Write `longestPalindrome(s)` returning the length of the longest palindrome that can be built using the characters of s (case-sensitive; each character may be used at most as many times as it appears).

challenges.title: Top-k frequent words
challenges.prompt: Write `topKWords(words, k)` returning the k most frequent words, sorted by frequency descending, ties broken by lexicographic (ascending) order.

challenges.title: Subarrays divisible by k
challenges.prompt: Write `subarraysDivByK(nums, k)` (k > 0) returning the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum is divisible by k. Values may be negative.

challenges.title: Distribute candies
challenges.prompt: Write `distributeCandies(nums)` where nums has even length. Return the maximum number of distinct kinds obtainable when exactly nums.length/2 elements are kept.

challenges.title: Longest harmonious subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `findLHS(nums)` returning the length of the longest subsequence whose maximum and minimum differ by exactly 1. Return 0 if no such subsequence exists.

challenges.title: Word pattern (bijection)
challenges.prompt: Write `wordPattern(pattern, s)` returning true iff there is a bijection between the letters of pattern and the space-separated words of s so that pattern describes s. Different letters must map to different words.

challenges.title: Sort characters by frequency
challenges.prompt: Write `frequencySortString(s)` returning s with its characters reordered by descending frequency; characters with equal frequency appear in ascending character order. The result contains each character as many times as it occurs.

challenges.title: Maximum depth of a binary tree

challenges.prompt: Write `runningMax(arr)` returning a new array where element i is the maximum of arr[0..i]. For an empty array return [].

challenges.title: Capped running total
challenges.prompt: Write `runningTotalCapped(arr, cap)` (non-negative numbers). Accumulate a running total, but the total can never exceed `cap` (clamp it at cap after each addition). Return the array of totals after each element.

challenges.title: Round half away from zero
challenges.prompt: Write `roundHalfAwayFromZero(x)` rounding x to the nearest integer, with ties (exact .5) rounded away from zero. E.g. 2.5 -> 3, -2.5 -> -3, -0.5 -> -1.

challenges.title: Round to nearest multiple
challenges.prompt: Write `roundToMultiple(n, m)` (m > 0) returning n rounded to the nearest multiple of m; halves round up (toward +infinity).

challenges.title: Inclusive range sum
challenges.prompt: Write `sumRange(a, b)` returning the sum of all integers from a to b inclusive. If a > b, return 0.

challenges.title: Sum of multiples of 3 or 5
challenges.prompt: Write `sumMultiples3or5(n)` returning the sum of all positive integers strictly below n that are multiples of 3 or 5.

challenges.title: Population count
challenges.prompt: Write `hammingWeight(n)` (n >= 0) returning the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of n. n may be larger than 2^32 but stays a safe integer.

challenges.title: Digit count in a base
challenges.prompt: Write `digitCountInBase(n, b)` (n >= 0, b >= 2) returning how many digits n has when written in base b. Note that 0 always has one digit.

challenges.title: Trailing zeros of factorial
challenges.prompt: Write `trailingZerosFactorial(n)` (n >= 0) returning the number of trailing zeros in n! without computing the factorial.

challenges.title: Sum of divisors
challenges.prompt: Write `sumDivisors(n)` (n >= 1) returning the sum of all positive divisors of n, including 1 and n itself.

challenges.title: Count divisors
challenges.prompt: Write `countDivisors(n)` (n >= 1) returning how many positive divisors n has.

challenges.title: Perfect number
challenges.prompt: Write `isPerfectNumber(n)` returning true if n equals the sum of its proper divisors (all positive divisors excluding n itself). E.g. 6 = 1+2+3.

challenges.title: GCD of an array
challenges.prompt: Write `gcdArray(arr)` returning the greatest common divisor of all integers in the non-empty array. The result must be non-negative.

challenges.title: Sum of even Fibonacci numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `sumEvenFibonacci(limit)` returning the sum of all even Fibonacci numbers that are less than or equal to `limit`. Use the sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...

challenges.title: Sum of divisors mod m
challenges.prompt: Write `sumDivisors(n, m)` returning the sum of all positive divisors of `n` (including 1 and n), taken modulo `m`. `n>=1`, `m` is a prime.

challenges.title: Count primes below n
challenges.prompt: Write `countPrimesBelow(n)` returning how many prime numbers are strictly less than `n`. `n>=0`.

challenges.title: Euler's totient
challenges.prompt: Write `totient(n)` returning Euler's totient phi(n): the count of integers in [1,n] coprime to n. `n>=1`, phi(1)=1.

challenges.title: Modular exponentiation
challenges.prompt: Write `modPow(base, exp, mod)` returning (base^exp) mod mod, using fast exponentiation. `base>=0`, `exp>=0`, `2<=mod<=1000003`. modPow(x,0,m)=1%m.

challenges.title: Modular inverse (extended gcd)
challenges.prompt: Write `modInverse(a, m)` returning the multiplicative inverse of `a` modulo `m` as an integer in [0, m). `a` and `m` are coprime, `m>=2`, `a>=1`. Use the extended Euclidean algorithm.

challenges.title: Linear congruence solver
challenges.prompt: Write `solveCongruence(a, b, m)` returning the smallest non-negative x with a*x ≡ b (mod m), or -1 if no solution exists. `m>=1`, `a>=0`, `0<=b<m`.

challenges.title: Binomial coefficient mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `nCrModP(n, r, p)` returning C(n, r) modulo prime `p`. `0<=r<=n`, `p` prime, `p<=1000003`, `n<100000`. Return 0 if r<0 or r>n.

challenges.title: Trailing zeros of n!
challenges.prompt: Write `trailingZerosFactorial(n)` returning the number of trailing zeros in n! (in base 10). `n>=0`.

challenges.title: Count divisors
challenges.prompt: Write `countDivisors(n)` returning the number of positive divisors of `n`. `n>=1`.

challenges.title: Count primes in range
challenges.prompt: Write `countPrimesInRange(lo, hi)` returning the number of primes p with lo<=p<=hi. `1<=lo<=hi`.

challenges.title: LCM of array mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `lcmMod(arr, p)` returning the least common multiple of the positive integers in `arr`, taken modulo prime `p`. Compute via prime factorization (max exponent per prime). `arr` non-empty, each element in [1, 100000].

challenges.title: CRT for two moduli
challenges.prompt: Write `crt2(a1, m1, a2, m2)` returning the smallest non-negative x with x≡a1 (mod m1) and x≡a2 (mod m2), or -1 if no solution exists. Moduli may share factors. `m1,m2>=1`, `0<=a1<m1`, `0<=a2<m2`.

challenges.title: Count numbers with given digit sum
challenges.prompt: Write `digitSumCount(N, s)` returning how many integers x in [0, N] have decimal digit sum exactly `s`. `N>=0`, `s>=0`.

challenges.title: Mobius function
challenges.prompt: Write `mobius(n)` returning the Möbius function μ(n): 0 if n is divisible by a perfect square > 1, otherwise (-1)^k where k is the number of distinct prime factors. μ(1)=1. `n>=1`.

challenges.title: Sum of integers coprime to n
challenges.prompt: Write `sumCoprime(n)` returning the sum of all integers in [1, n] that are coprime to `n`. For n=1 the answer is 1. `n>=1`.

challenges.title: Count divisible by any prime (inclusion-exclusion)
challenges.prompt: Write `countDivisibleByAny(n, primes)` returning how many integers in [1, n] are divisible by at least one prime in the distinct list `primes`. Use inclusion-exclusion. `n>=0`, `primes` has up to 15 distinct primes.

challenges.title: Population count (large integers)
challenges.prompt: Write `popcount(n)` returning the number of set bits in the binary representation of the non-negative integer `n`. `n` may be as large as 2^53.

challenges.title: Total set bits up to n
challenges.prompt: Write `totalSetBits(n)` returning the total number of set bits across all integers from 0 to n inclusive. `n>=0`, up to 2^40.

challenges.title: Gray code of n
challenges.prompt: Write `grayCode(n)` returning the n-th standard reflected binary Gray code value (n XOR (n>>1)) as a number. `n>=0`, up to 2^50.

challenges.title: Gray code to binary
challenges.prompt: Write `grayToBinary(g)` returning the integer whose reflected-binary Gray code is `g` (the inverse of gray coding). `g>=0`, up to 2^50.

challenges.title: Reverse bits within width
challenges.prompt: Write `reverseBits(n, width)` returning the integer formed by reversing the lowest `width` bits of `n` (bits above `width` are ignored). `0<=n<2^width`, `1<=width<=50`.

challenges.title: XOR of 0..n
challenges.prompt: Write `xorUpTo(n)` returning 0 XOR 1 XOR 2 XOR ... XOR n. Use the closed-form pattern (do not loop for huge n). `n>=0`, up to 10^12.

challenges.title: Single number (others appear thrice)
challenges.prompt: Write `singleNumberThrice(arr)` where every value appears exactly three times except one value that appears once; return that single value. Values are non-negative and may exceed 2^32. `arr` non-empty.

challenges.title: Hamming distance
challenges.prompt: Write `hammingDistance(a, b)` returning the number of bit positions where non-negative integers `a` and `b` differ. Values may exceed 2^32.

challenges.title: Next number with same popcount
challenges.prompt: Write `nextSameSetBits(n)` returning the smallest integer greater than `n` with the same number of set bits (the classic 'snoob'). `n>=1`, and the answer stays within 2^53.

challenges.title: Bitwise AND of range
challenges.prompt: Write `andRange(m, n)` returning the bitwise AND of all integers from m to n inclusive. `0<=m<=n`, values up to 2^45.

challenges.title: Count integers with no adjacent set bits
challenges.prompt: Write `countNoAdjacentBits(n)` returning how many integers x in [0, n] have no two adjacent set bits in binary. `n>=0`, up to 2^45.

challenges.title: Number to base-k digits
challenges.prompt: Write `toBaseK(n, k)` returning an array of the digits of `n` in base `k`, most-significant first. For n=0 return [0]. `n>=0`, `2<=k<=36`, n up to 2^50.

challenges.title: Base-k digits to number
challenges.prompt: Write `fromBaseK(digits, k)` returning the integer value of digit array `digits` (most-significant first) interpreted in base `k`. Empty array is 0. `2<=k<=36`, result within 2^50.

challenges.title: Flip all bits within width
challenges.prompt: Write `flipBits(n, width)` returning the value of `n` with all of its lowest `width` bits flipped (one's complement within a fixed width). `0<=n<2^width`, `1<=width<=50`.

challenges.title: Lowest set bit position
challenges.prompt: Write `lowestSetBit(n)` returning the 0-indexed position of the least-significant set bit of `n`, or -1 if `n` is 0. `n>=0`, up to 2^52.

challenges.title: Highest set bit position
challenges.prompt: Write `highestSetBit(n)` returning the 0-indexed position of the most-significant set bit of `n` (i.e. floor(log2 n)), or -1 if `n` is 0. `n>=0`, up to 2^52.

challenges.title: Catalan number mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `catalanMod(n, p)` returning the n-th Catalan number modulo prime `p`. `0<=n<=100000`, `p` prime, `p<=1000003`.

challenges.title: Grid paths with obstacles mod p
challenges.prompt: Write `gridPaths(grid, p)` returning the number of paths from top-left to bottom-right of `grid` moving only right or down, avoiding cells marked 1 (0 = free), modulo prime `p`. If start or end is blocked, return 0. `grid` is a non-empty rectangular array of 0/1.

challenges.title: Ways to make change (combinations) mod p
challenges.prompt: Write `changeWays(coins, amount, p)` returning the number of distinct multisets of `coins` summing to `amount` (order does not matter), modulo prime `p`. Coins are positive integers; `amount>=0`.

challenges.title: Derangements mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `derangements(n, p)` returning the number of permutations of n elements with no fixed point (subfactorial !n) modulo prime `p`. `n>=0`, D(0)=1. `p` prime.

challenges.title: Stirling numbers of the second kind mod p
challenges.prompt: Write `stirling2(n, k, p)` returning S(n,k), the number of ways to partition a set of n elements into k non-empty subsets, modulo prime `p`. `n,k>=0`, S(0,0)=1. `p` prime.

challenges.title: Bell numbers mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `bellNumber(n, p)` returning the n-th Bell number (number of partitions of an n-element set) modulo prime `p`, computed via the Bell triangle. `n>=0`, B(0)=1. `p` prime.

challenges.title: Row of Pascal's triangle (exact)
challenges.prompt: Write `pascalRow(n)` returning the n-th row of Pascal's triangle [C(n,0),...,C(n,n)] as an exact integer array. `0<=n<=56` (all values fit safely).

challenges.title: Multinomial coefficient mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `multinomial(counts, p)` returning (sum!)/(c1! c2! ... ) modulo prime `p`, where `counts` is a non-empty array of non-negative integers and sum = sum of counts (< 100000). `p` prime, `p<=1000003`.

challenges.title: Binary strings without consecutive ones
challenges.prompt: Write `countBinaryNoConsec(n)` returning the number of binary strings of length `n` that contain no two consecutive 1s. `n>=0`; the empty string (n=0) counts as 1.

challenges.title: Count subsets with given sum
challenges.prompt: Write `subsetSumCount(arr, target)` returning the number of subsets of `arr` (each element used at most once) whose elements sum to exactly `target`. Elements are positive integers; `target>=0`. The empty subset sums to 0.

challenges.title: Binomial mod small prime (Lucas)
challenges.prompt: Write `lucasNCr(n, r, p)` returning C(n, r) modulo the small prime `p`, where `n` may be far larger than `p`. Use Lucas' theorem. `0<=r<=n`, `p` prime, `p<=100`. Return 0 if r<0 or r>n.

challenges.title: Integer partitions
challenges.prompt: Write `partitionCount(n)` returning the number of partitions of the integer `n` (unordered sums of positive integers). p(0)=1. `0<=n<=100` (fits safely).

challenges.title: Fibonacci mod prime
challenges.prompt: Write `fibMod(n, p)` returning the n-th Fibonacci number modulo prime `p`, with F(0)=0, F(1)=1. `n>=0`, up to 10^7. `p` prime.

challenges.title: Range sum with point set
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeSumPointSet(arr, ops)`. Process each op on a working copy of `arr` in order: `["set", i, v]` sets `arr[i] = v`; `["sum", l, r]` returns the sum of `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE of both ends. Return an array with one result per `"sum"` op, in order.

challenges.title: Range minimum queries
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeMin(arr, queries)`. Each query is `[l, r]`; return the minimum of `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE of both ends. Return an array of answers, one per query, in order.

challenges.title: Range max with point set
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeMaxSet(arr, ops)`. Process each op on a working copy of `arr`: `["set", i, v]` sets `arr[i] = v`; `["max", l, r]` returns the maximum of `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE of both ends. Return an array with one result per `"max"` op, in order.

challenges.title: Count of smaller after self
challenges.prompt: Write `countSmaller(nums)` returning an array `counts` where `counts[i]` is the number of indices `j > i` with `nums[j] < nums[i]` (STRICTLY smaller). Equal values do not count. Return the array.

challenges.title: Count range sum in [lower, upper]
challenges.prompt: Write `countRangeSum(nums, lower, upper)` returning the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose sum `S` satisfies `lower <= S <= upper` (both bounds INCLUSIVE). Return the count.

challenges.title: Number of inversions
challenges.prompt: Write `countInversions(nums)` returning the number of pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `nums[i] > nums[j]` (STRICTLY greater). Equal values are NOT inversions. Return the count.

challenges.title: Range add, range sum
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeAddRangeSum(arr, ops)`. Process ops in order on a working copy: `["add", l, r, v]` adds `v` to every element in `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE; `["sum", l, r]` returns the sum of `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE. Return an array with one result per `"sum"` op, in order.

challenges.title: Sliding window maximum
challenges.prompt: Write `slidingWindowMax(nums, k)` returning an array of the maximum of every contiguous window of exactly `k` elements, left to right. The output has `nums.length - k + 1` entries. Assume `1 <= k <= nums.length`.

challenges.title: Longest well-performing interval
challenges.prompt: Write `longestWPI(hours)`. A day is tiring if `hours[i] > 8` (STRICTLY). A well-performing interval is a contiguous subarray in which the number of tiring days is STRICTLY greater than the number of non-tiring days. Return the length of the longest well-performing interval (0 if none).

challenges.title: Subarray sums divisible by K
challenges.prompt: Write `subarraysDivByK(nums, k)` returning the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose sum is divisible by `k` (`k >= 1`). Sums may be negative; a sum is divisible by `k` when it is a multiple of `k` (including 0). Return the count.

challenges.title: Max rectangle sum no larger than K
challenges.prompt: Write `maxRectSumNoLargerThanK(matrix, k)` returning the maximum sum of any non-empty axis-aligned sub-rectangle whose sum is `<= k` (INCLUSIVE). It is guaranteed at least one sub-rectangle has sum `<= k`. Return that maximum sum.

challenges.title: Kth largest in a stream
challenges.prompt: Write `kthLargestStream(k, initial, adds)`. Start with the multiset `initial`. For each value `x` in `adds`, insert `x`, then record the k-th largest value currently in the multiset (1-indexed: the largest is the 1st). Duplicates count as distinct entries. It is guaranteed the multiset has at least `k` elements after each insertion. Return the array of recorded values, one per add.

challenges.title: My Calendar I
challenges.prompt: Write `myCalendar(bookings)`. Each booking is a half-open interval `[start, end)`. Process bookings in order: a booking succeeds (returns true) if it does NOT overlap any previously-succeeded booking, otherwise it fails (returns false) and is not stored. Two intervals overlap iff they share a region of positive length; touching at an endpoint (e.g. `[1,2)` and `[2,3)`) does NOT overlap. Return the array of booleans.

challenges.title: 2D range sum queries
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeSum2D(matrix, queries)`. Each query is `[r1, c1, r2, c2]`; return the sum of all cells `matrix[r][c]` with `r1 <= r <= r2` and `c1 <= c <= c2` (all bounds INCLUSIVE). Return an array of answers, one per query, in order.

challenges.title: Subarray sum equals K (count)
challenges.prompt: Write `subarraySumEqualsK(nums, k)` returning the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose sum equals exactly `k`. `k` and the values may be negative or zero. Return the count.

challenges.title: Shortest subarray with sum at least K
challenges.prompt: Write `shortestSubarrayAtLeastK(nums, k)` returning the length of the SHORTEST non-empty contiguous subarray whose sum is `>= k` (INCLUSIVE), or `-1` if none exists. `nums` may contain negative numbers. Return the length or -1.

challenges.title: Reverse pairs
challenges.prompt: Write `reversePairs(nums)` returning the number of pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]` (STRICTLY greater). Equality (`nums[i] === 2 * nums[j]`) does NOT count. Return the count.

challenges.title: Sliding window minimum
challenges.prompt: Write `slidingWindowMin(nums, k)` returning an array of the minimum of every contiguous window of exactly `k` elements, left to right. The output has `nums.length - k + 1` entries. Assume `1 <= k <= nums.length`.

challenges.title: Range XOR queries
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeXor(arr, queries)`. Each query is `[l, r]`; return the bitwise XOR `arr[l] ^ arr[l+1] ^ ... ^ arr[r]` INCLUSIVE of both ends. Values are non-negative integers. Return an array of answers, one per query, in order.

challenges.title: Range GCD queries
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeGcd(arr, queries)`. Each query is `[l, r]`; return the greatest common divisor of `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE of both ends. All values are positive integers. Return an array of answers, one per query, in order.

challenges.title: Subarrays with bounded maximum
challenges.prompt: Write `numSubarrayBoundedMax(nums, left, right)` returning the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose maximum element is in the INCLUSIVE range `[left, right]` (i.e. `left <= max <= right`). Return the count.

challenges.title: Max subarray sum no larger than K
challenges.prompt: Write `maxSubarrayNoLargerThanK(nums, k)` returning the maximum sum of any non-empty CONTIGUOUS subarray whose sum is `<= k` (INCLUSIVE). The subarray may start at ANY index. It is guaranteed at least one subarray has sum `<= k`. Return that maximum sum.

challenges.title: My Calendar II (no triple booking)
challenges.prompt: Write `myCalendarTwo(bookings)`. Each booking is a half-open interval `[start, end)`. Process bookings in order: a booking succeeds (returns true) unless adding it would cause any point to be covered by three or more bookings (a triple booking), otherwise it fails (returns false) and is not stored. Intervals overlap only over a region of positive length; touching endpoints do NOT overlap. Return the array of booleans.

challenges.title: Longest subarray with sum K
challenges.prompt: Write `maxLenSubarraySumK(nums, k)` returning the length of the LONGEST contiguous subarray whose sum equals exactly `k`, or `0` if none exists. Values and `k` may be negative or zero. Return the length.

challenges.title: Range add, point query
challenges.prompt: Write `rangeAddPointGet(arr, ops)`. Process ops in order on a working copy: `["add", l, r, v]` adds `v` to every element in `arr[l..r]` INCLUSIVE of both ends; `["get", i]` returns the current value of `arr[i]`. Return an array with one result per `"get"` op, in order.

challenges.title: Text justification (full)
challenges.prompt: Write `fullJustify(words, maxWidth)` that formats `words` into lines of exactly `maxWidth` characters, fully (left+right) justified. Greedily pack as many words per line as fit with at least one space between them. Distribute extra spaces so that left gaps get more than or equal to right gaps. The LAST line and any line with a single word are left-justified: words separated by one space, padded with trailing spaces to `maxWidth`. Return an array of the lines.

challenges.title: Text justification (left)
challenges.prompt: Write `leftJustify(words, maxWidth)` that packs `words` greedily into lines (as many as fit with single spaces between them, never exceeding `maxWidth`), separates words by exactly one space, and pads EVERY line — including the last — on the right with spaces to exactly `maxWidth`. Return an array of the padded lines.

challenges.title: Run-length compress
challenges.prompt: Write `rleCompress(s)` that compresses `s` by runs: replace each maximal run of a repeated character with the character followed by the run length, but a run of length 1 is written as just the character (NO count). Example: 'aaabbc' -> 'a3b2c'. Empty string returns ''.

challenges.title: Run-length decode
challenges.prompt: Write `rleDecode(s)` that decodes a run-length string. The string is a sequence of pairs: a single character followed by a (possibly multi-digit) decimal count, meaning that character repeated `count` times. Example: 'a3b2c1' -> 'aaabbc', 'a12' -> twelve a's. Assume every character is followed by at least one digit.

challenges.title: Count and say
challenges.prompt: Write `countAndSay(n)` returning the n-th term (1-indexed) of the count-and-say sequence. Term 1 is '1'. Each next term is formed by reading the previous term as consecutive runs, emitting the run length followed by the digit for each run. So '1' -> '11' -> '21' -> '1211' -> '111221' ...

challenges.title: Basic calculator (precedence)
challenges.prompt: Write `calculate(s)` that evaluates an arithmetic expression string containing non-negative integers and the operators + - * / separated by optional spaces (no parentheses). Multiplication and division bind tighter than addition and subtraction. Integer division truncates toward zero. Example: '3+2*2' -> 7, ' 3/2 ' -> 1.

challenges.title: Basic calculator (parentheses)
challenges.prompt: Write `calculateP(s)` that evaluates an expression string of non-negative integers, the operators + and -, parentheses, and optional spaces. Parentheses may be nested and a subtraction may negate a whole parenthesized group. Example: '1-(2+3)' -> -4, '2-(5-6)' -> 3.

challenges.title: Simplify Unix path
challenges.prompt: Write `simplifyPath(path)` that converts an absolute Unix-style path to its canonical form. '.' means current directory, '..' means go up one level (no-op at root), repeated slashes collapse to one, and there is no trailing slash unless the path is root. Note: a name like '...' is an ordinary directory, not a parent reference. The result always starts with '/'.

challenges.title: Compare version numbers
challenges.prompt: Write `compareVersion(v1, v2)` comparing two dot-separated version strings. Compare revisions left to right as integers (ignore leading zeros). Missing trailing revisions count as 0, so '1.0' equals '1' and '1.0.0.0' equals '1'. Return -1 if v1 < v2, 1 if v1 > v2, else 0.

challenges.title: Parse ternary expression
challenges.prompt: Write `parseTernary(expr)` that evaluates a nested ternary expression built from the characters 'T', 'F', digits, '?' and ':'. Conditions are 'T' (true) or 'F' (false). The '?:' operator is RIGHT-associative and every operand is a single character. Return the resulting single-character string. Example: 'T?2:3' -> '2', 'F?1:T?4:5' -> '4'.

challenges.title: Decode nested repeats
challenges.prompt: Write `decodeString(s)` decoding a string with the rule k[encoded] meaning `encoded` repeated k times. Encodings may be nested and k may be multi-digit. The input is always valid and k is a positive integer (there are no digits in the plain text). Example: '3[a2[c]]' -> 'accaccacc', '2[abc]3[cd]ef' -> 'abcabccdcdcdef'.

challenges.title: Validate IP address
challenges.prompt: Write `validIP(ip)` returning 'IPv4', 'IPv6', or 'Neither'. IPv4: four decimal groups 0-255 joined by '.', each 1-3 digits with no leading zeros (except '0' itself). IPv6: eight groups joined by ':', each 1-4 hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f, A-F). Anything else is 'Neither'.

challenges.title: Column number to title
challenges.prompt: Write `convertToTitle(n)` converting a positive integer to its spreadsheet column title (bijective base-26). 1 -> 'A', 26 -> 'Z', 27 -> 'AA', 28 -> 'AB', 52 -> 'AZ', 701 -> 'ZY', 702 -> 'ZZ'.

challenges.title: Column title to number
challenges.prompt: Write `titleToNumber(s)` converting a spreadsheet column title to its number (bijective base-26). 'A' -> 1, 'B' -> 2, 'Z' -> 26, 'AA' -> 27, 'AB' -> 28, 'ZY' -> 701.

challenges.title: Roman to integer
challenges.prompt: Write `romanToInt(s)` converting a Roman numeral to an integer. Values: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000. When a smaller value precedes a larger one it is subtracted (IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, CM=900). Example: 'MCMXCIV' -> 1994.

challenges.title: Integer to roman
challenges.prompt: Write `intToRoman(n)` converting an integer (1..3999) to its Roman numeral, using the subtractive forms IV(4), IX(9), XL(40), XC(90), CD(400), CM(900). Example: 4 -> 'IV', 1994 -> 'MCMXCIV'.

challenges.title: Tic-tac-toe evaluate
challenges.prompt: Write `evaluate(board)` for a 3x3 board given as an array of three rows, each a length-3 array of 'X', 'O', or '' (empty). Return 'X' or 'O' if that mark has three in a row (any row, column, or either diagonal), 'Draw' if the board is full with no winner, or 'Pending' if there is an empty cell and no winner. Assume the board is a valid reachable position.

challenges.title: Robot final state
challenges.prompt: Write `robot(cmd)` simulating a robot on an infinite grid starting at (0,0) facing North. Directions are encoded 0=N,1=E,2=S,3=W. Process each character of `cmd`: 'G' moves one step forward (North is +y, East is +x), 'R' turns 90 degrees right (clockwise), 'L' turns 90 degrees left (counter-clockwise). Return the final state as [x, y, dir].

challenges.title: Robot bounded in circle

challenges.title: String to integer (atoi)

challenges.title: Valid parenthesis string with wildcard
challenges.prompt: Write `checkValid(s)` returning true if the string of '(', ')' and '*' can be a valid parenthesization. Each '*' may be treated as '(', ')', or an empty string. challenges.title: Backspace string
challenges.prompt: Write `buildString(s)` that returns the text produced by typing `s` where '#' is a backspace that deletes the previous character (or does nothing if the text is empty). Example: 'ab#c' -> 'ac', 'a##c' -> 'c', '###a' -> 'a'.

challenges.title: Longest common prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `lcp(strs)` returning the longest common prefix shared by ALL strings in the array `strs`. If there is no common prefix return ''. An empty array returns '' and a single-element array returns that element.

challenges.title: Multiply number strings
challenges.prompt: Write `multiply(a, b)` returning the product of two non-negative integers given as decimal strings, as a decimal string. Do not use BigInt. The result must have no leading zeros, and multiplying by '0' yields '0'. Example: '123' * '456' -> '56088'.

challenges.title: Add number strings
challenges.prompt: Write `addStrings(a, b)` returning the sum of two non-negative integers given as decimal strings, as a decimal string. Do not use BigInt. The strings may have different lengths and there are no leading zeros in the input. Example: '99' + '1' -> '100'.

challenges.title: Reverse words
challenges.prompt: Write `reverseWords(s)` that reverses the order of words in `s`. A word is a maximal run of non-space characters. Collapse multiple spaces, and strip leading and trailing spaces, so the result has words separated by exactly one space and no surrounding spaces. Example: '  the sky  is blue  ' -> 'blue is sky the'.

challenges.title: ZigZag conversion
challenges.prompt: Write `convert(s, rows)` writing `s` in a zigzag pattern across the given number of `rows` (going down then diagonally up, repeating) and then reading it off row by row. With rows=1 the string is returned unchanged. Example: convert('PAYPALISHIRING', 3) -> 'PAHNAPLSIIGYIR'.

challenges.title: Spiral matrix order
challenges.prompt: Write `spiralOrder(matrix)` returning all elements of the matrix (an array of row arrays, not necessarily square) in clockwise spiral order starting from the top-left. Example: [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] -> [1,2,3,6,9,8,7,4,5].

challenges.title: Rotate matrix 90 clockwise
challenges.prompt: Write `rotate(matrix)` returning a NEW n x n matrix that is `matrix` rotated 90 degrees clockwise. The top row of the input becomes the right column of the output. Example: [[1,2],[3,4]] -> [[3,1],[4,2]].

challenges.title: Game of Life next state
challenges.prompt: Write `gameOfLife(board)` returning a NEW board that is the next generation of Conway's Game of Life. `board` is a grid of 0 (dead) and 1 (live). All cells update simultaneously from the current state: a live cell with 2 or 3 live (8-directional) neighbors survives, a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbors becomes live, everything else is dead.

challenges.title: Count words
challenges.prompt: Write `countWords(s)` returning the number of words in `s`. A word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters. Leading/trailing/repeated whitespace (spaces, tabs) must not create empty words. Empty or all-whitespace input has 0 words.

challenges.title: Reverse word order
challenges.prompt: Write `reverseWords(s)` returning the words of `s` in reverse order, joined by single spaces. Collapse any runs of whitespace; ignore leading/trailing whitespace. Empty/all-whitespace input returns "".

challenges.title: Alphanumeric palindrome
challenges.prompt: Write `isPalindrome(s)` returning true if `s` reads the same forwards and backwards when ignoring case and all non-alphanumeric characters. Empty string is a palindrome.
