challenges.title: Run-length encode
challenges.prompt: Write `runLengthEncode(s)` that encodes each maximal run of a repeated character as the character followed by its count (the count is always included, even when 1). E.g. "aaabbc" -> "a3b2c1". Empty input returns "".

challenges.title: Run-length decode
challenges.prompt: Write `runLengthDecode(s)` that decodes a string of character+count pairs, where counts may have multiple digits. E.g. "a3b2" -> "aaabb", "a12" -> "aaaaaaaaaaaa". Empty input returns "".

challenges.title: Caesar cipher
challenges.prompt: Write `caesarCipher(s, shift)` that shifts each letter by `shift` positions (wrapping within its case), leaving non-letters unchanged. `shift` may be negative or larger than 26.

challenges.title: Count vowels
challenges.prompt: Write `countVowels(s)` returning the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in `s`, counting both uppercase and lowercase. 'y' is not a vowel.

challenges.title: Title case words
challenges.prompt: Write `titleCase(s)` where words are separated by single spaces. Return `s` with each word's first character uppercased and the rest of the word lowercased.

challenges.title: Most frequent character
challenges.prompt: Write `mostFrequentChar(s)` returning the character that occurs most often in `s`. On a tie, return the character whose first occurrence comes earliest. Empty input returns "".

challenges.title: Letter frequency map
challenges.prompt: Write `charFrequency(s)` returning an object mapping each letter (case-insensitive, lowercased) to its count. Only alphabetic characters are counted; non-letters are ignored. Keys must appear in the order each letter is first seen.

challenges.title: Anagram check
challenges.prompt: Write `isAnagram(a, b)` returning true if `a` and `b` are anagrams of each other, ignoring spaces and letter case.

challenges.title: Count overlapping occurrences
challenges.prompt: Write `countOverlapping(s, sub)` returning the number of times `sub` occurs in `s`, counting overlapping occurrences. If `sub` is empty, return 0.

challenges.title: First non-repeating character
challenges.prompt: Write `firstNonRepeating(s)` returning the first character (in original case) that appears exactly once when counting case-insensitively. If every character repeats, return "".

challenges.title: Normalize whitespace
challenges.prompt: Write `normalizeSpaces(s)` that collapses every run of whitespace into a single space and trims leading/trailing whitespace.

challenges.title: Parse leading integer
challenges.prompt: Write `parseLeadingInt(s)` that skips leading spaces, then reads an optional sign (+ or -) followed by digits, and returns the integer value. If no digits are found, return 0. Characters after the number are ignored.

challenges.title: Parse CSV line
challenges.prompt: Write `parseCsvLine(line)` that splits a CSV line on commas into an array of fields. A field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas; the surrounding quotes are removed and the inner commas are kept. (No escaped quotes inside fields.)

challenges.title: Render template
challenges.prompt: Write `renderTemplate(tmpl, vars)` that replaces every occurrence of `{{key}}` with `vars[key]` (as a string). Placeholders whose key is not in `vars` are left literally as `{{key}}`.

challenges.title: camelCase to snake_case
challenges.prompt: Write `toSnakeCase(s)` that converts camelCase to snake_case by inserting an underscore before each uppercase letter (except at the start) and lowercasing everything. E.g. "helloWorld" -> "hello_world".

challenges.title: snake_case to camelCase
challenges.prompt: Write `toCamelCase(s)` that converts snake_case to camelCase. Split on underscores, ignoring empty parts from consecutive/leading/trailing underscores; the first non-empty part stays as-is and each subsequent part is capitalized. E.g. "hello_world" -> "helloWorld".

challenges.title: Word counts
challenges.prompt: Write `wordCounts(s)` returning an object mapping each word to its number of occurrences. Words are maximal runs of [a-z0-9] after lowercasing (any other character is a separator). Keys must be in order of first appearance.

challenges.title: Longest word
challenges.prompt: Write `longestWord(s)` returning the longest word (words are separated by whitespace). On a tie, return the word that appears first. Empty/all-whitespace input returns "".

challenges.title: Reverse letters only
challenges.prompt: Write `reverseLetters(s)` that reverses only the alphabetic characters of `s`, leaving every non-letter in its original position. E.g. "a1bc" -> "c1ba".

challenges.title: ROT13
challenges.prompt: Write `rot13(s)` applying the ROT13 substitution to every letter (both cases), leaving non-letters unchanged.

challenges.title: Valid brackets
challenges.prompt: Write `validBrackets(s)` returning true if all bracket characters ()[]{} in `s` are correctly matched and nested. Non-bracket characters are ignored.

challenges.title: Collapse adjacent duplicates
challenges.prompt: Write `removeAdjacentDuplicates(s)` that collapses each run of consecutive identical characters into a single character. E.g. "aabbcc" -> "abc", "aaabbba" -> "aba".

challenges.title: Sum of digit characters
challenges.prompt: Write `sumDigits(s)` returning the sum of the values of all individual digit characters in `s`. E.g. "a1b2c3" -> 6, "12" -> 3.

challenges.title: Extract integers
challenges.prompt: Write `extractIntegers(s)` returning an array of all integers found in `s`, in order, as numbers. A leading '-' immediately before digits denotes a negative number. E.g. "a-5b12" -> [-5, 12].

challenges.title: Word initials
challenges.prompt: Write `initials(s)` returning the uppercased first letter of each word joined together. Words are separated by whitespace; ignore leading/trailing/repeated whitespace. Empty/all-whitespace input returns "".

challenges.title: Pig Latin (one word)
challenges.prompt: Write `pigLatin(word)` for a single lowercase word. If it begins with a vowel (a,e,i,o,u), append "way". Otherwise move the entire leading run of consonants to the end and append "ay". E.g. "smile" -> "ilesmay", "apple" -> "appleway". Empty input returns "".

challenges.title: String rotation
challenges.prompt: Write `isRotation(a, b)` returning true if `b` is a rotation of `a` (some cyclic shift of `a` equals `b`). Two equal strings (including two empty strings) are rotations of each other.

challenges.title: Interleave characters
challenges.prompt: Write `interleave(a, b)` that interleaves the characters of `a` and `b` (a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], ...), then appends the remaining characters of whichever string is longer. E.g. "abc"+"12" -> "a1b2c".

challenges.title: Swap case
challenges.prompt: Write `swapCase(s)` returning `s` with each uppercase letter made lowercase and each lowercase letter made uppercase. Non-letters are unchanged.

challenges.title: Count upper and lower
challenges.prompt: Write `countCase(s)` returning an object `{upper, lower}` with the counts of uppercase and lowercase letters in `s`. Non-letter characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) are not counted.

challenges.title: Thousands separators
challenges.prompt: Write `addThousands(n)` returning the integer `n` as a string with commas grouping every three digits from the right. Handle negative numbers (e.g. -123456 -> "-123,456") and never produce a leading comma.

challenges.title: Reverse vowels
challenges.prompt: Write `reverseVowels(s)` that reverses the order of the vowels (a,e,i,o,u in either case) in `s` while leaving all other characters in place. E.g. "Aa" -> "aA".

challenges.title: Longest common prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonPrefix(arr)` returning the longest string that is a prefix of every string in `arr`. Return "" if the array is empty or the strings share no common prefix.

challenges.title: Most common word
challenges.prompt: Write `mostCommonWord(s)` returning the most frequent word. Words are maximal runs of [a-z0-9] after lowercasing (any other character separates words). On a tie, return the word that appears first. Empty input returns "".

challenges.title: Count sentences
challenges.prompt: Write `countSentences(s)` returning the number of sentences. Sentences are separated by one or more terminators from the set . ! ? — a run of consecutive terminators ends a single sentence. Text after the last terminator with no terminator still counts as a sentence. Blank segments do not count.

challenges.title: Truncate with ellipsis
challenges.prompt: Write `truncate(s, n)` that returns `s` unchanged if its length is at most `n`; otherwise return the first `n` characters followed by "...".

challenges.title: Isogram check
challenges.prompt: Write `isIsogram(s)` returning true if no letter appears more than once, comparing letters case-insensitively. Non-letter characters are ignored. Empty string is an isogram.

challenges.title: Longest common prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonPrefix(words)` returning the longest string that is a prefix of every word in `words`. Return `""` if there is no common prefix or the list is empty.

challenges.title: Count words with prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `countPrefix(words, queries)`. For each query string, return how many words in `words` have that query as a prefix. Return an array of counts aligned with `queries`.

challenges.title: Word search II
challenges.prompt: Write `findWords(grid, words)`. `grid` is an array of equal-length strings (rows of letters). A word is found if it can be formed by a path of horizontally/vertically adjacent cells where each cell is used at most once. Return the sorted array of distinct words from `words` that can be found.

challenges.title: Replace words (shortest root)
challenges.prompt: Write `replaceWords(roots, sentence)`. `sentence` is a string of space-separated words. Replace each word with the SHORTEST root in `roots` that is a prefix of it; if several roots are prefixes, use the shortest. If no root is a prefix, keep the word unchanged. Return the resulting space-separated string.

challenges.title: Longest buildable word

challenges.title: Search suggestions
challenges.prompt: Write `suggestedProducts(products, searchWord)`. challenges.title: Palindrome pairs

challenges.title: Count distinct prefixes
challenges.prompt: Write `countDistinctPrefixes(words)` returning the number of distinct non-empty prefixes across all words (equivalently, the number of nodes, excluding the root, in a trie built from the words).

challenges.title: Stream checker
challenges.prompt: Write `streamChecker(words, letters)`. `letters` is an array of single characters queried one at a time, forming a growing stream. For each query, return `true` if any string in `words` is a suffix of the stream so far. Return the array of booleans, one per query.

challenges.title: Map sum prefixes
challenges.prompt: Write `mapSum(ops)`. `ops` is a list of operations processed in order: `["insert", key, value]` sets `key` to `value` (overwriting any previous value), and `["sum", prefix]` asks for the total of the values of all keys that start with `prefix`. challenges.title: Camelcase matching
challenges.prompt: Write `camelMatch(queries, pattern)`. challenges.title: Shortest unique prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `shortestUniquePrefix(words)`. `words` are distinct and none is a prefix of another. For each word return its shortest prefix that no other word also has as a prefix. Return the array of prefixes aligned with the input order.

challenges.title: Longest common suffix
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonSuffix(words)` returning the longest string that is a suffix of every word in `words`. Return `""` if there is no common suffix or the list is empty.

challenges.title: Pairs sharing a k-prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `countKPrefixPairs(words, k)` returning the number of unordered pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` whose two words share a common prefix of length at least `k` (both words must actually have at least `k` matching leading characters).

challenges.title: Sum of prefix scores
challenges.prompt: Write `sumPrefixScores(words)`. The score of a word is the sum, over each of its non-empty prefixes, of the number of words in the list (including itself) that have that prefix. Return an array of scores aligned with the input order.

challenges.title: Word filter (prefix + suffix)
challenges.prompt: Write `wordFilter(words, queries)`. Each query is a pair `[prefix, suffix]`. For each query return the largest index `i` such that `words[i]` starts with `prefix` and ends with `suffix`, or `-1` if none. Return the array of indices aligned with `queries`.

challenges.title: Add & search word (wildcards)
challenges.prompt: Write `wordDictionary(ops)`. `ops` is processed in order: `["add", word]` stores a word, and `["search", pattern]` returns `true` if any stored word exactly matches `pattern`, where a `.` in the pattern matches any single character. challenges.title: Magic dictionary
challenges.prompt: Write `magicSearch(dict, queries)`. For each query return `true` if you can change EXACTLY one character of the query (keeping the same length) so that it equals some word in `dict`. Return an array of booleans aligned with `queries`.

challenges.title: Index pairs of a string
challenges.prompt: Write `indexPairs(text, words)` returning all pairs `[start, end]` (inclusive indices) such that `text.substring(start, end + 1)` equals some word in `words`. Include overlapping occurrences. Return the list sorted by `start`, then by `end`.

challenges.title: Concatenated words
challenges.prompt: Write `concatenatedWords(words)` returning the sorted list of words that can be formed by concatenating two or more shorter words from the list (a word may not use itself as a whole, but shorter words may be reused). Return the sorted array of such words.

challenges.title: Autocomplete top-k by frequency
challenges.prompt: Write `topKPrefix(words, prefix, k)`. Treat repeated occurrences in `words` as frequency. Among the DISTINCT words that start with `prefix`, return up to `k` of them ranked by frequency (highest first), breaking ties by lexicographic order. Return the array of words.

challenges.title: Words that prefix another
challenges.prompt: Write `wordsPrefixOfOther(words)` returning the sorted list of distinct words that are a proper prefix of at least one other word in the list.

challenges.title: Remove subfolders
challenges.prompt: Write `removeSubfolders(folders)`. Each folder is an absolute path like `"/a/b"`. Remove every folder that is a subfolder of another folder in the list (folder `X` is a subfolder of `Y` if `X` starts with `Y + "/"`). Return the remaining folders sorted lexicographically.

challenges.title: Count words that prefix a string
challenges.prompt: Write `countPrefixesOf(words, s)` returning how many words in `words` are a prefix of the string `s` (count each list entry separately, including duplicates).

challenges.title: Count words by prefix and suffix
challenges.prompt: Write `countPrefixSuffix(words, queries)`. Each query is a pair `[prefix, suffix]`. For each query, count how many words in `words` start with `prefix` AND end with `suffix`. Return an array of counts aligned with `queries`.

challenges.title: Trie insert / search / startsWith
challenges.prompt: Write `trieOps(ops)`. challenges.title: Short encoding length
challenges.prompt: Write `shortEncodingLength(words)`. A word need not be encoded separately if it is a suffix of another (distinct) word. challenges.title: Replace words (longest root)
challenges.prompt: Write `replaceLongestRoot(roots, sentence)`. `sentence` is a string of space-separated words. Replace each word with the LONGEST root in `roots` that is a prefix of it; if several roots are prefixes, use the longest. If no root is a prefix, keep the word unchanged. Return the resulting space-separated string.

challenges.title: Count prefix-conflict pairs
challenges.prompt: Write `countConflictPairs(words)` returning the number of unordered pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` such that one of the two words is a prefix of the other (equal words count, since a word is a prefix of itself).

challenges.title: Lexicographic top-k for a prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `lexTopKPrefix(words, prefix, k)` returning up to `k` distinct words that start with `prefix`, chosen as the lexicographically smallest such words, in ascending lexicographic order.

challenges.title: Count components (adjacency list)

challenges.title: Count components (edge list)
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs (edges may repeat), return the number of connected components. Isolated nodes count as their own component.

challenges.title: Number of provinces
challenges.prompt: Given an n x n symmetric matrix `isConnected` where isConnected[i][j] === 1 means cities i and j are directly connected (and 0 otherwise, with isConnected[i][i] === 1), return the number of provinces. A province is a maximal group of directly or indirectly connected cities.

challenges.title: Number of islands (4-directional)
challenges.prompt: Given a 2D grid of 0s (water) and 1s (land), return the number of islands. An island is a maximal group of 1s connected 4-directionally (up/down/left/right). Diagonal adjacency does NOT connect. Return 0 for an empty grid.

challenges.title: Redundant connection

If several edges could be removed, return the one that appears LAST in the input.

challenges.title: Accounts merge (count)

challenges.title: Earliest moment everyone connected

challenges.title: Largest component size

challenges.title: Groups remaining after each union

challenges.title: Satisfiability of equality equations

challenges.title: Regions cut by slashes

challenges.title: Most stones removed
challenges.prompt: `stones` is a list of [row, col] positions of stones on an infinite grid (all distinct). challenges.title: Number of islands II (online)

challenges.title: Graph valid tree

challenges.title: Count unreachable pairs

challenges.title: Making a large island
challenges.prompt: Given an n x n grid of 0s and 1s, you may change AT MOST one 0 into a 1. Return the size of the largest island (4-directionally connected 1s) you can obtain. If the grid is all 1s, return the total count.

challenges.title: Servers that communicate
challenges.prompt: Given an m x n binary `grid` where grid[i][j] === 1 means a server sits at (i,j), a server can communicate with another server if they are in the same row or the same column. Return the number of servers that can communicate with AT LEAST one other server.

challenges.title: Similar string groups
challenges.prompt: `strs` is a list of strings that are all anagrams of one another (duplicates may appear). challenges.title: Redundant directed connection

Using these relations, return `baseStr` with every character replaced by the lexicographically smallest character in its equivalence class.

challenges.title: Count complete connected components
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs (no self loops or duplicate edges), a connected component is 'complete' if there is an edge between every pair of its vertices. Return the number of complete connected components.

challenges.title: Count connected pairs
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs (duplicates possible), return the number of unordered pairs (i,j) with i<j that are in the same connected component.

challenges.title: Number of islands (8-directional)
challenges.prompt: Given a 2D grid of 0s and 1s, return the number of islands where an island is a maximal group of 1s connected in any of the 8 directions (including diagonals). Return 0 for an empty grid.

challenges.title: Is the graph fully connected
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 (n >= 1) and an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs, return true if every node is reachable from every other node (the graph is a single connected component), else false.

challenges.title: Components of size at least k
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1, an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs, and an integer `k`, return the number of connected components whose size is at least k. Isolated nodes are components of size 1.

challenges.title: Size of a node's component
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1, an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs, and a node `q`, return the number of nodes in the connected component that contains q (including q itself).

challenges.title: Batch connectivity queries
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1, an undirected `edges` list of [u,v] pairs, and a list of `queries` [a,b], return an array of booleans where the i-th entry is true iff a and b are in the same connected component (a node is always connected to itself).

challenges.title: Online cycle detection
challenges.prompt: Given `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected `edges` list processed IN ORDER, return an array of booleans: the i-th entry is true iff adding edges[i] connects two nodes that were already in the same component (i.e., it creates a cycle). A self-loop [x,x] always creates a cycle.

challenges.title: Count sub-islands
challenges.prompt: You are given two m x n binary grids `grid1` and `grid2` (same dimensions). An island in grid2 is a maximal group of 1s connected 4-directionally. Return the number of islands in grid2 that are 'sub-islands': every cell of the island is also land (1) in grid1.

challenges.title: Dijkstra: shortest distance
challenges.prompt: Write `shortestDist(n, edges, src, dst)`. The directed weighted graph has nodes 0..n-1; `edges` is an array of `[u, v, w]` (edge u->v with weight w>=0). Return the length of the shortest path from `src` to `dst`, or -1 if `dst` is unreachable.

challenges.title: Dijkstra: all shortest distances
challenges.prompt: Write `allDist(n, edges, src)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` with w>=0. Return an array of length n where entry i is the shortest distance from `src` to node i, or -1 if node i is unreachable (`src` itself is 0).

challenges.title: Bellman-Ford with negatives
challenges.prompt: Write `bfDist(n, edges, src, dst)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` where w may be negative. Return the shortest distance from `src` to `dst`; return -1 if `dst` is unreachable, and the string "NEG" if the shortest distance is undefined because `dst` is reachable from a negative-weight cycle that is itself reachable from `src`.

challenges.title: Detect a negative cycle
challenges.prompt: Write `hasNegCycle(n, edges)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` with possibly-negative w. Return `true` if the graph contains any negative-weight cycle (anywhere, not only reachable from node 0), else `false`.

challenges.title: Minimum spanning tree weight (Kruskal)
challenges.prompt: Write `mstWeight(n, edges)`. Undirected weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]`. Return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree, or -1 if the graph is not connected (single node with no edges has weight 0).

challenges.title: Minimum spanning tree weight (Prim)
challenges.prompt: Write `primMST(n, edges)`. Undirected weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` (each edge connects u and v both ways). Return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree, or -1 if the graph is disconnected.

challenges.title: Count strongly connected components
challenges.prompt: Write `sccCount(n, edges)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]` (edge u->v). Return the number of strongly connected components.

challenges.title: Lexicographically smallest topological order
challenges.prompt: Write `topoOrder(n, edges)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]` (u must come before v). Return the lexicographically smallest valid topological ordering as an array, or -1 if the graph has a cycle (no valid order).

challenges.title: Shortest path with exactly k edges
challenges.prompt: Write `exactK(n, edges, src, dst, k)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` with w>=0. Return the minimum total weight of a walk from `src` to `dst` using exactly `k` edges (nodes/edges may repeat), or -1 if no such walk exists. When k is 0, the answer is 0 only if src equals dst.

challenges.title: Network delay time
challenges.prompt: Write `netDelay(n, times, src)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `times` = `[u, v, w]` (signal travels u->v in time w>=0). Return the time for a signal from `src` to reach ALL nodes (the maximum over shortest distances), or -1 if some node is unreachable.

challenges.title: Cheapest flights within k stops
challenges.prompt: Write `cheapFlights(n, flights, src, dst, k)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `flights` = `[u, v, w]` (price w). Return the cheapest total price from `src` to `dst` using at most `k` intermediate stops (so at most k+1 edges), or -1 if not reachable within the limit.

challenges.title: Connected components after unions
challenges.prompt: Write `countComponents(n, ops)`. Start with n isolated nodes 0..n-1. `ops` is an array of `[a, b]` union operations that merge the components of a and b. Return the number of connected components after applying all operations (redundant unions must not reduce the count).

challenges.title: Bipartite check
challenges.prompt: Write `isBipartite(n, edges)`. Undirected graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]`. Return `true` if the whole graph (all components) is bipartite (2-colorable), else `false`.

challenges.title: Count articulation points
challenges.prompt: Write `artPoints(n, edges)`. Undirected graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]`. Return the number of articulation points (cut vertices) — nodes whose removal increases the number of connected components. Handle disconnected graphs.

challenges.title: Shortest cycle length (undirected)
challenges.prompt: Write `shortestCycle(n, edges)`. Simple undirected graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]`. Return the number of edges in the shortest cycle (its girth), or -1 if the graph is acyclic. The cycle may lie in any component.

challenges.title: Number of shortest paths
challenges.prompt: Write `countShortest(n, edges, src, dst)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` with w>=0. Return how many distinct shortest paths exist from `src` to `dst`. Return 0 if `dst` is unreachable; if src equals dst the answer is 1. Answers stay within safe integer range.

challenges.title: Minimum bottleneck path
challenges.prompt: Write `bottleneck(n, edges, src, dst)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]`. Among all paths from `src` to `dst`, return the minimum possible value of the largest edge weight on the path (the minimax bottleneck), or -1 if `dst` is unreachable. If src equals dst the answer is 0.

challenges.title: Bipartite check with component count
challenges.prompt: Write `bipartiteReason(n, edges)`. Undirected graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]`. If the graph is bipartite return `[true, 0]`. Otherwise return `[false, k]` where k is the number of connected components that are NOT bipartite (contain an odd cycle).

challenges.title: Shortest directed cycle (girth)
challenges.prompt: Write `shortestDirectedCycle(n, edges)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]` (edge u->v). Return the number of edges in the shortest directed cycle, or -1 if the graph is acyclic. A single edge u->v is NOT a cycle unless the reverse edge v->u also exists.

challenges.title: All-pairs shortest-distance sum
challenges.prompt: Write `apspSum(n, edges)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` with w>=0. Compute the shortest distance between every ordered pair (i, j) with i != j, and return the sum over all such pairs that are reachable (unreachable pairs contribute nothing).

challenges.title: Largest strongly connected component
challenges.prompt: Write `largestSCC(n, edges)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]`. Return the number of nodes in the largest strongly connected component.

challenges.title: Longest chain in a DAG
challenges.prompt: Write `longestChain(n, edges)`. Directed graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]` (u->v). If the graph is a DAG, return the number of nodes on the longest path (a single node counts as 1). If the graph has a cycle, return -1.

challenges.title: Shortest path with at most k edges
challenges.prompt: Write `atMostK(n, edges, src, dst, k)`. Directed weighted graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v, w]` with w>=0. Return the minimum total weight of a path from `src` to `dst` using at most `k` edges, or -1 if no such path exists. If src equals dst the answer is 0 (zero edges).

challenges.title: Count bridges
challenges.prompt: Write `bridges(n, edges)`. Undirected graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]`. Return the number of bridges — edges whose removal increases the number of connected components. Handle disconnected graphs.

challenges.title: Count connected components
challenges.prompt: Write `ccCount(n, edges)`. Undirected graph, nodes 0..n-1, `edges` = `[u, v]` (connects u and v both ways). Return the number of connected components.

challenges.title: Count occurrences (with overlaps)
challenges.prompt: Write `countOverlapping(text, pat)` returning how many times `pat` occurs in `text`, counting OVERLAPPING occurrences (e.g. "aa" occurs 3 times in "aaaa"). Return 0 when `pat` is empty.

challenges.title: Longest palindromic substring (length)
challenges.prompt: Write `longestPalindromeLength(s)` returning the length of the longest palindromic substring of `s`. Return 0 for the empty string.

challenges.title: Longest palindromic substring (canonical)
challenges.prompt: Write `longestPalindrome(s)` returning the longest palindromic substring of `s`. If several share the maximum length, return the leftmost one. Return "" for the empty string.

challenges.title: Count palindromic substrings
challenges.prompt: Write `countPalindromicSubstrings(s)` returning the total number of palindromic substrings of `s`, counting each occurrence (position) separately. Single characters count.

challenges.title: Longest common substring (length)
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonSubstring(a, b)` returning the length of the longest CONTIGUOUS substring appearing in both `a` and `b`. Return 0 if there is none.

challenges.title: Longest common subsequence (length)
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonSubsequence(a, b)` returning the length of the longest common SUBSEQUENCE (characters in order, not necessarily contiguous) of `a` and `b`.

challenges.title: Minimum insertions to make palindrome
challenges.prompt: Write `minInsertionsPalindrome(s)` returning the fewest character insertions (at any positions) needed to turn `s` into a palindrome.

challenges.title: Smallest repeating period
challenges.prompt: Write `smallestPeriod(s)` returning the length of the smallest unit `u` such that `s` is `u` repeated a whole number of times (>=1). If `s` has no shorter repetition, return its length. Return 0 for the empty string.

challenges.title: Wildcard matching (? and *)
challenges.prompt: Write `wildcardMatch(s, p)` returning true iff pattern `p` matches the whole string `s`. In `p`, '?' matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence (including empty). All other characters match literally.

challenges.title: Longest happy prefix
challenges.prompt: Write `longestHappyPrefix(s)` returning the longest PROPER prefix of `s` that is also a suffix of `s` (a border). Return "" if none exists.

challenges.title: Count distinct substrings
challenges.prompt: Write `distinctSubstrings(s)` returning the number of DISTINCT non-empty substrings of `s`. `s` has length <= 60.

challenges.title: Minimum window substring
challenges.prompt: Write `minWindow(s, t)` returning the smallest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t` including multiplicities. If several share the minimum length, return the leftmost. Return "" if none exists or `t` is empty.

challenges.title: Repeated substring pattern
challenges.prompt: Write `repeatedSubstringPattern(s)` returning true iff `s` can be constructed by taking some substring and concatenating two or more copies of it.

challenges.title: Longest palindromic subsequence
challenges.prompt: Write `longestPalindromicSubsequence(s)` returning the length of the longest palindromic SUBSEQUENCE (characters in order, not necessarily contiguous) of `s`.

challenges.title: Shortest palindrome length
challenges.prompt: Write `shortestPalindromeLength(s)` returning the length of the shortest palindrome obtainable by prepending characters to the FRONT of `s`. Return 0 for the empty string.

challenges.title: Edit distance (Levenshtein)
challenges.prompt: Write `editDistance(a, b)` returning the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, or substitutions needed to transform `a` into `b`.

challenges.title: Longest repeated substring
challenges.prompt: Write `longestRepeatedSubstring(s)` returning the length of the longest substring that occurs at least twice in `s`. The two occurrences MAY overlap. Return 0 if no substring repeats.

challenges.title: Count anagram occurrences
challenges.prompt: Write `countAnagramOccurrences(s, p)` returning how many substrings of `s` are anagrams (permutations) of `p`. Both strings consist of lowercase letters a-z.

challenges.title: Count distinct subsequences equal to target
challenges.prompt: Write `countSubsequences(s, t)` returning the number of distinct subsequences of `s` that equal `t`. The answer is guaranteed to fit in a standard JS number (< 1e12).

challenges.title: Is rotation
challenges.prompt: Write `isRotation(a, b)` returning true iff `b` is a rotation of `a` (some cyclic shift of `a` equals `b`). Two empty strings are rotations of each other.

challenges.title: Longest common substring (canonical)
challenges.prompt: Write `longestCommonSubstringStr(a, b)` returning the longest contiguous substring common to both `a` and `b`. If several share the maximum length, return the one whose occurrence ends earliest in `a` (i.e. the leftmost such match in `a`). Return "" if none.

challenges.title: Regular expression matching (. and *)
challenges.prompt: Write `regexMatch(s, p)` returning true iff pattern `p` matches the ENTIRE string `s`. '.' matches any single character; '*' matches zero or more of the character immediately preceding it. Other characters match literally.

challenges.title: Find all occurrences (overlapping)
challenges.prompt: Write `findAllOccurrences(text, pat)` returning an array of the starting indices (ascending) of every occurrence of `pat` in `text`, counting OVERLAPPING occurrences. Return [] when `pat` is empty.

challenges.title: Count distinct palindromic substrings
challenges.prompt: Write `countDistinctPalindromicSubstrings(s)` returning the number of DISTINCT non-empty palindromic substrings of `s` (each distinct string counted once, regardless of how many times it occurs).

challenges.title: Longest substring without repeating characters
challenges.prompt: Write `longestUnique(s)` returning the length of the longest substring of `s` containing no repeated character.
